Evidence:
Obtain the identity register naming each identity type, its holding directory and its population size.
Collect the identity lifecycle procedure mapping each event to its authoritative trigger and the identity action taken.
Gather the shared and service identity register with justification, named owner and credential custody per entry.
Retrieve leaver identity records carrying both the trigger timestamp and the disablement timestamp.
Obtain the reconciliation output listing orphaned and dormant identities with the decision on each.

Analysis:
Export the live account population from each named directory and compare its size with the figure registered.
Trace a sample of leavers from the authoritative people record to disablement and compute the elapsed time from the stated trigger.
Check that each shared or service identity has a current employee as owner and a justification that still describes a live need.
Test whether the reconciliation source is the authoritative people, contractor and service record, not the directory reconciled against itself.
Establish that dormant identities close with a disablement or a dated exception rather than an open status.

Output:
A per-directory count of live identities against the registered population.
The distribution of leaver disablement intervals with the outliers named.
A list of shared and service identities lacking a current owner or a live justification.

title.en: List the identity types in use and the directories that hold each

description.en: Enumerate the categories of identity the organisation issues — employee, contractor, temporary, third-party, customer, service and shared identities — and record which directory, application account store or cloud tenancy holds each category. Identities held outside the central directory are the ones that survive a leaver process. Evidence: the identity register naming each identity type, its holding directory and the population size.

evidenceHint.en: Identity register naming each identity type, its holding directory and its population size

title.en: Define the lifecycle events that create, change and disable an identity, and the trigger for each

description.en: Write the procedure connecting a real-world event to an identity action: hire, contract start, internal transfer, extended absence, contract end and departure, and for each name the authoritative source that signals it and the identity action it forces. Cover contractor and third-party identities, which usually have a different signalling source from employees. Evidence: the identity lifecycle procedure mapping each event to its authoritative trigger and the resulting create, amend or disable action.

evidenceHint.en: Identity lifecycle procedure mapping each event to its authoritative trigger and identity action

title.en: Record the justification and named human owner for every shared and service identity

description.en: Work through the shared accounts, service accounts and machine identities found in the register; for each, record why an individual identity could not be used, the human accountable for it, the systems it reaches and how its credential is held. Where no justification survives contact, schedule the identity for replacement. Evidence: the shared and service identity register, one row per identity with its justification, its named owner and its credential custody arrangement.

evidenceHint.en: Shared and service identity register with justification, named owner and credential custody per identity

title.en: Disable identities on the leaver trigger and record the elapsed time from trigger to disablement

description.en: On each departure or contract end, disable the individual's identities across every directory in the register, and record both the moment the authoritative trigger fired and the moment each identity was disabled. Recording the interval is what makes the delay visible and improvable. Evidence: the leaver identity records for the period, naming the person, each identity disabled, the trigger timestamp and the disablement timestamp.

evidenceHint.en: Leaver identity records naming each identity disabled, with trigger timestamp and disablement timestamp

title.en: Reconcile active identities against the authoritative people, contractor and service records

description.en: Extract the active identities from every directory in the register and match them against the current people record, the contractor schedule and the service identity register. List identities with no matching current holder, dormant identities, and holders with identities in directories their role does not require, and drive each to disablement or a recorded exception. Evidence: the reconciliation output listing orphaned and dormant identities with the disablement or exception decision on each.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation output listing orphaned and dormant identities with the disablement or exception decision per line

templates.title: Authentication information
templates.description: Manage allocation and use of authentication info
templates.objective: To ensure credentials reach only a confirmed recipient, are strong enough for what they protect, and are replaced or withdrawn once exposed or no longer needed.
templates.successCriteria:
Every kind of authentication information in use is registered against the systems relying on it, its holders and where it is held.
No credential is issued or replaced without a recorded authorisation and a confirmed recipient, system-held credentials included.
Each kind carries a stated strength requirement and validity period, with a per-system note of how that is upheld.
Exposed or outlived credentials are replaced, and no credential supplied with a product or created at installation remains usable.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of authentication information by system and kind, with holder populations and storage locations.
Collect the issuance and replacement procedure for person-held and system-held credentials, covering authorisation, recipient confirmation and first use.
Gather the strength and validity requirement statement per kind, with the per-system note of how it is upheld.
Retrieve the period's log of issues, replacements and withdrawals, and the record of credentials replaced after exposure.
Obtain the check record stating, per system, whether a supplied or installation credential remains usable.

Analysis:
Sample issuance entries and confirm each names the requester, the performer and the confirmation method actually used.
Compare the stated strength and validity requirements with the configuration enforced on each system named.
Trace a known exposure through to the replacement record and the systems it touched.
Witness an authentication attempt with a documented default credential on a sample of systems to test the check's claim.
Assess whether service account secrets and API keys travel the same issuance route as credentials issued to people.

Output:
A register-to-system coverage statement for authentication information.
Sampled issuance records with the recipient confirmation evidenced or missing on each.
A per-system verdict on supplied and installation-time credentials.

title.en: List the kinds of authentication information in use and where each is held

description.en: For every system a person or a process signs in to, record the kinds of authentication information it accepts — secrets the holder chooses, credentials issued to a named holder, and credentials used by systems and scripts with no person behind them — and where each is kept once it has been issued. Attach the register, one row per system and kind, naming the holder population and the place of custody.

evidenceHint.en: Register of authentication information by system and kind, naming the holder population and where the credential is held

title.en: Set out how a request is authorised and the recipient confirmed before authentication information is issued or replaced

description.en: Write the procedure covering first issue and every later replacement, for both kinds of entry on the register. Where the credential has a person behind it: what establishes that the person asking is the holder, how the credential reaches them without passing through anyone else's hands or records, whether it must be replaced by the holder before it can be used for real work, and what is done when a request arrives and the holder cannot be reached in the usual way. Where the credential belongs to a system, service or script with no person behind it: who may request one, what authorises the request, the named role accountable for the credential once it exists, and how it is placed into the system that will use it without being exposed on the way. Attach the issuance and replacement procedure, covering both kinds.

evidenceHint.en: Issuance and replacement procedure covering person-held and system-held credentials: what authorises the request, how the recipient is confirmed, and first use

title.en: State what makes each kind of authentication information strong enough and how long it stays valid

description.en: For each kind on the register, record the requirement — what an acceptable secret or credential must be, whether it may be reused anywhere else, and the point at which it ceases to be valid — and note against each system whether the requirement is upheld by the system itself or depends on the holder observing it, since the second needs a different kind of assurance. Attach the requirement statement together with the per-system note of how it is upheld.

evidenceHint.en: Requirement statement per kind of authentication information, with a per-system note of how it is upheld

title.en: Record each issue, replacement and withdrawal of authentication information with the confirmation performed

description.en: Every time authentication information is allocated, replaced or withdrawn, record who asked, who carried it out, how the holder was confirmed and the date, writing the entry as the act is done rather than reconstructing it afterwards. Attach the log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Log of issues, replacements and withdrawals for the period, each naming the requester, the performer and the confirmation made

title.en: Replace authentication information that has been exposed or has outlived its purpose

description.en: When a credential is disclosed in the course of support, turns up somewhere it should not be held, is left over from work that has ended, or is held by someone no longer entitled to it, replace or withdraw it and record what was done. Attach the replacement record naming each credential, the reason it was replaced, the systems affected and the date.

evidenceHint.en: Replacement record naming each credential replaced or withdrawn, the reason, the systems affected and the date

title.en: Establish that credentials supplied with a product or created at installation can no longer be used

description.en: Work the register system by system and establish for each that any credential that arrived with the product or was created when it was installed has been removed or replaced — by demonstrating that it is refused, or from the system's own list of holders. Record the systems where this could not be established as findings rather than as passes. Attach the check record, one row per system with the outcome.

evidenceHint.en: Check record with one row per system stating what was checked and whether a supplied credential remains usable

templates.title: Access rights
templates.description: Provision, review and revoke access rights
templates.objective: To ensure the rights a person actually holds are the rights an authorised approver granted, and that they contract when the person's role changes or ends.
templates.successCriteria:
Every access profile each system offers is catalogued with what that profile permits.
Each profile has a required approver and a stated minimum content an approval must carry.
Grants made in the period rest on an approval recorded before the grant and kept with it.
Role changes and departures produced a decision on every profile held with the removals executed, and rights no approval or review decision supports are removed or formally accepted.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the entitlement catalogue naming each system, the profiles it offers and what each permits.
Collect the approval map giving the required approver and required approval contents for every catalogued profile.
Gather the grants made in the period, each naming the person, the profile, the approval relied on and who executed it.
Retrieve the role-change and departure records showing profiles held, the keep or remove decision on each and the removals executed.
Obtain the completed access review, including the privileged recertification result carried into it.

Analysis:
Pull a live entitlement export from a sample of systems and compare the profiles held against the catalogue.
Test each sampled grant for an approval dated before the grant and given by the approver the map requires.
Follow role changers to confirm the rights their former role carried were withdrawn, not merely added to.
Check the review for holders kept without a named reviewer, and for remove decisions with no matching removal.
Reconcile rights held against approvals and review decisions and account for every right neither supports.

Output:
A held-versus-catalogued profile comparison per sampled system.
A list of grants made without a qualifying prior approval.
An exception list of unsupported rights with the removal or acceptance recorded against each.

title.en: Catalogue the access profiles each system offers and what each one permits

description.en: For every system, list the roles, groups or entitlement sets a person can be given and state in plain words what each one lets the holder see and do, marking those that grant administrative or otherwise unrestricted reach. Attach the entitlement catalogue; without it neither an approver nor a reviewer has anything to judge against.

evidenceHint.en: Entitlement catalogue naming each system, each profile it offers and what that profile permits

title.en: Record who must approve each profile and what the approval has to state

description.en: Map every profile in the catalogue to the person or role whose agreement is needed before anyone holds it, and set out what an approval must contain — the person, the profile, the business reason, and how long it is needed for. State how the approval is captured so that it can be produced later against the grant it authorised. Attach the approval map covering every profile in the catalogue.

evidenceHint.en: Approval map giving the required approver and the required contents of an approval for every catalogued profile

title.en: Grant access only against a recorded approval and keep the approval with the grant

description.en: For each grant made in the period record the person, the system, the profile, the approval relied on and who carried the grant out, and turn away requests that arrive without an approval rather than granting first and papering over it afterwards. Attach the grants made in the period, each tied to the approval that authorised it.

evidenceHint.en: Grants made in the period, each naming the person, the profile, the approval relied on and who executed it

title.en: Withdraw the access a person no longer needs when they change role or leave

description.en: On each move or departure, list the profiles the person holds, decide keep or remove against what their new position requires, and execute the removals — paying particular attention to access that survives their account being closed, such as membership of groups, access to shared repositories and mailboxes, rights on locally held accounts, and access delegated to others on their behalf. A move that only adds is the accumulation this task exists to stop. Attach the records showing profiles held before, the decision on each and the removals executed.

evidenceHint.en: Role-change and departure records showing profiles held before, the keep or remove decision on each and the removals executed

title.en: Put every holder of each non-administrative profile to its system owner for a keep or remove decision

description.en: When the access review falls due, give each system owner the current holders of every profile in their systems that the catalogue does not mark as granting administrative or otherwise unrestricted reach, and require an explicit keep or remove decision against each named person, refusing blanket approvals covering a whole list. The profiles the catalogue does mark are recertified where privileged access rights are managed: take that recertification's result into this review and record that it was taken in, rather than deciding those holders again here. Where a system offers no profile outside the marked ones, record that and the recertification carried in. Return the removals for execution and confirm they were carried out. Attach the completed review showing the reviewer, the decision per holder, the removals executed, and the privileged result carried in.

evidenceHint.en: Completed access review showing the reviewer, a keep or remove decision per holder, the executed removals, and the privileged recertification result carried in

title.en: Account for every right held that no approval or review decision supports

description.en: Take the rights actually held in each system and match them against the approvals recorded and the decisions returned by the last review. List every right with nothing behind it, every administrative profile whose holders were never approved, and every holder whose right outlived the reason it was granted, then drive each line to removal or to an acceptance recorded against a named owner. Attach the comparison with a disposition on every line.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of held rights against approvals and review decisions, with a removal or recorded acceptance on every line

templates.title: Information security in supplier relationships
templates.objective: To ensure the security expected of a supplier is set by the risk its access carries and is settled before that supplier is given anything to access.
templates.successCriteria:
Every supplier that reaches information or information systems is on the register with its access route and business owner.
Each registered supplier carries a risk tier assigned against stated classification criteria.
The assurance required before onboarding is written per tier, so the requirement is known before a supplier is chosen.
Suppliers onboarded in the period were assessed against their tier before access was granted, and no engaged third party is missing from the register.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the supplier register with the access route and business owner recorded per supplier.
Collect the classification criteria and the risk tier assigned to each registered supplier.
Gather the tiered supplier security requirements document.
Retrieve the completed pre-onboarding assessments for suppliers onboarded during the period.
Obtain the reconciliation of the register against externally held accounts and engaged third parties.

Analysis:
Compare the register against payables, procurement records and externally granted accounts to find suppliers with access but no entry.
Re-apply the classification criteria to a sample of suppliers and test whether the assigned tier follows from them.
Check that each pre-onboarding assessment answers every requirement its tier sets rather than a general questionnaire.
Compare the date of each assessment with the date access was first granted to that supplier.
Establish how unregistered suppliers found in the reconciliation were handled and whether the register was corrected.

Output:
A register completeness statement naming the unregistered suppliers found.
Sampled tier assignments with agreement or disagreement recorded per supplier.
A timeline of assessment against first access for each supplier onboarded in the period.

title.en: Compile a register of suppliers that access information or information systems

description.en: List each supplier, the information or system it reaches, how it reaches it (network access, hosted data, on-site presence, staff augmentation) and the internal business owner. Attach the register; suppliers with no access to information are out of scope and should be excluded deliberately, not overlooked.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier register with access route and business owner per supplier

title.en: Classify each registered supplier by the risk its access presents

description.en: Apply a written criterion — sensitivity of information reached, depth of access, dependence of the business on the service — and record the resulting tier against each supplier. Attach the register carrying the tier column plus the criteria used to assign it.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier register with assigned risk tier and the classification criteria

title.en: State the security assurance required before onboarding a supplier in each tier

description.en: For every tier, write down what must be obtained before access is granted — assessment questionnaire, certification or audit report, technical review, contractual commitments. Attach the tiered requirements so an onboarding decision can be checked against a stated bar.

evidenceHint.en: Tiered supplier security requirements document

title.en: Assess each new supplier against its tier's requirements before access is granted

description.en: Run the assurance activity the tier demands, record the findings and any accepted shortfalls, and note who approved granting access. Attach the completed assessment for each supplier onboarded in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Completed pre-onboarding assessment per supplier onboarded in the period

title.en: Reconcile the supplier register against externally held accounts and engaged third parties

description.en: Compare the register with the external identities present in the organisation's systems and with third parties actually engaged by the business, to find suppliers that gained access without being registered. Attach the reconciliation and the disposition of each supplier found outside the register.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing unregistered suppliers found and how each was handled

templates.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
templates.description: Include security requirements in supplier contracts
templates.objective: To ensure the security obligations placed on a supplier are written into the agreement that binds it, so they outlast the people who negotiated them and can be enforced.
templates.successCriteria:
A required-clause set exists and states which clauses apply at each supplier tier.
The standard supplier contract template carries those clauses, so a new agreement reaches the supplier with them already in it.
The clause-coverage matrix shows, supplier by required clause, what each active agreement actually contains.
Suppliers onboarded in the period have an executed agreement or amendment filed against their register entry, and every clause gap has a recorded decision-maker.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the required-clause set and its mapping to supplier tier.
Collect the standard supplier contract template with the security clauses marked.
Gather the clause-coverage matrix of active agreements against required clauses.
Retrieve the executed agreements or security amendments filed for suppliers onboarded in the period.
Obtain the clause-gap list with the decision and decision-maker recorded on each gap.

Analysis:
Read a sample of executed agreements and verify each matrix entry against the contract text rather than the template used.
Test whether the clause set covers subcontracting, incident notification, return or deletion of information and right of audit.
Confirm the template the contracting team works from today is the version carrying the marked clauses.
Check that agreements pre-dating the clause set appear in the matrix and were not set aside as legacy.
Assess whether each gap decision was taken by someone able to accept the exposure it leaves.

Output:
A clause-by-clause coverage result for the sampled agreements.
A list of matrix entries the contract text contradicts.
An account of open clause gaps with the accepting decision-maker named.

title.en: Draw up the set of security clauses a supplier agreement must contain

description.en: Derive the clause set from the supplier tiers — confidentiality, permitted use of information, incident notification, subcontracting consent, personnel screening, return or deletion of information on exit, and the right to verify. State which clauses apply to which tier. Attach the clause set.

evidenceHint.en: Required-clause set, mapped to supplier tier

title.en: Insert the required security clauses into the standard supplier contract template

description.en: Amend the organisation's standard agreement and any framework or purchase-order terms so the clause set is the default rather than negotiated case by case. Attach the updated template with the security clauses marked and the version date visible.

evidenceHint.en: Updated contract template with the security clauses marked

title.en: Record which required clauses each active supplier agreement actually contains

description.en: Read every in-force agreement for registered suppliers and mark, clause by clause, whether it is present, absent or weakened by negotiation. Attach the coverage matrix of supplier against clause — this is what turns the template into an assertion about signed contracts.

evidenceHint.en: Clause-coverage matrix, supplier by required clause

title.en: File the executed agreement or amendment for each supplier onboarded in the period

description.en: For every supplier taken on, store the signed agreement (or the signed security amendment to an existing one) against its register entry so the contract is retrievable without asking the business owner. Attach the executed documents filed for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Executed agreements or security amendments filed against register entries

title.en: Resolve each active agreement that is missing a required clause

description.en: Take every gap from the coverage matrix and record the route chosen — renegotiation at renewal, a side letter, a compensating technical or operational measure, or a documented acceptance — together with who decided. Attach the gap list with a disposition against every entry.

evidenceHint.en: Clause-gap list with the decision and decision-maker for each gap

templates.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
templates.objective: To ensure the risk carried in through purchased ICT, its upstream components and its delivery is judged before adoption and re-judged as the supply chain shifts.
templates.successCriteria:
Each acquired ICT product and service is listed with its supplier, where it runs and the service that depends on it.
Dependency declarations have been sought from every ICT supplier, with non-responses recorded rather than left blank.
Security acceptance criteria are applied before adoption, with a decision and decision-maker recorded per acquisition.
Delivered software and firmware are verified for authenticity and integrity before deployment, and entries failing the criteria carry a recorded outcome.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the ICT component list showing product or service, supplier, where it runs and the dependent service.
Collect the per-supplier dependency declarations of subcontractors and upstream components, including the record of non-responses.
Gather the ICT acquisition security acceptance criteria.
Retrieve the completed acceptance records for ICT adopted in the period, each with its decision and decision-maker.
Obtain the signature or checksum verification records for the releases deployed.

Analysis:
Compare the component list against deployed software inventories and cloud subscriptions to find ICT acquired outside the route.
Test a sample of acceptance records against the criteria and identify criteria marked met with nothing behind them.
Follow one dependency declaration to the subcontractors it names and consider whether their failure would reach the dependent service.
Re-perform a signature or checksum verification on a deployed release and compare the result with the one recorded.
Check whether non-responding suppliers were escalated or accepted, and on whose authority.

Output:
A list of ICT in use but absent from the component list.
Sampled acceptance decisions with the criteria left unevidenced on each.
Re-performed verification results set beside the recorded ones.

title.en: List the ICT products and services acquired and the supplier behind each

description.en: Cover hardware, purchased and open-source software, cloud components and outsourced development or support. Record the supplier, where the component runs and which business service depends on it. Attach the ICT component list; it is the population every other task here works over.

evidenceHint.en: ICT component list: product or service, supplier, where it runs, dependent service

title.en: Obtain from each ICT supplier the subcontractors and upstream components it relies on

description.en: Ask each supplier on the list to declare its own sub-suppliers, sub-processors and any critical third-party components embedded in what it delivers, and record where a supplier declines or cannot answer. Attach the per-supplier dependency declarations.

evidenceHint.en: Per-supplier dependency declarations, including non-responses

title.en: Set the security acceptance criteria applied before an ICT product or service is adopted

description.en: State what an acquisition must satisfy: provenance and authenticity checks, a secure default configuration, vulnerability disclosure and patching commitments, notification of subcontractor change, and a component inventory where the supplier can provide one. Attach the criteria document.

evidenceHint.en: ICT acquisition security acceptance criteria

title.en: Record the acceptance check performed for each ICT product or service adopted in the period

description.en: For every acquisition, work the criteria, record the evidence the supplier provided against each one, and note the accept, accept-with-conditions or reject decision and who made it. Attach the completed acceptance records.

evidenceHint.en: Completed acceptance record per acquisition with the decision and decision-maker

title.en: Verify the authenticity and integrity of delivered software and firmware before deployment

description.en: Check the supplier's signature or published checksum against what was received, from a source independent of the download itself, and record the result before the artefact reaches a production system. Attach the verification records for releases deployed in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Signature or checksum verification records per release deployed

title.en: Review the ICT component list for entries that no longer meet the acceptance criteria

description.en: Check each entry for end of vendor support, unresolved disclosed vulnerabilities, and notified changes of subcontractor or ownership. Record the action taken for each entry that fails — replace, upgrade, isolate, or formally accept. Attach the review with a per-entry outcome.

evidenceHint.en: ICT component review with the outcome recorded against every entry

templates.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
templates.objective: To ensure a supplier's delivery and security posture stay visible through the engagement, and that changes it makes to its service are judged before they take effect.
templates.successCriteria:
What each supplier owes by way of service and security reporting is recorded, with the frequency due and the recipient.
Reports falling due in the period were received and reviewed, with findings raised where their content warranted it.
Every supplier-notified service change is logged with an impact assessment made before the change took effect.
Suppliers above the risk threshold held their periodic service review, closing with agreed actions and named owners.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the supplier monitoring schedule naming the report due, its frequency and its recipient for each supplier.
Collect the procedure by which a supplier-notified service change is assessed before it takes effect.
Gather the supplier reports received in the period with the review notes and any findings raised.
Retrieve the supplier change log with the impact assessment outcome recorded per change.
Obtain the service review records for suppliers above the risk threshold, with agreed actions and owners.

Analysis:
Compare reports due under the schedule with reports actually received, and identify those never chased.
Read a sample of review notes to establish whether the report's content was tested or the report merely filed.
Set the date of each logged assessment against the date its change took effect.
Confirm findings raised from reports and reviews were tracked to a conclusion rather than recorded once.
Test whether the risk threshold used to call service reviews matches the tiering applied to the same suppliers elsewhere.

Output:
A due-against-received report matrix per supplier.
A list of service changes assessed after they took effect, with the interval on each.
The open actions from service reviews with their owners and ages.

title.en: Record what each supplier owes by way of service and security reporting

description.en: Per supplier, list the reports, attestations, certification renewals and performance figures due, the frequency of each and the internal recipient. Attach the monitoring schedule; a supplier owing nothing should say so explicitly rather than be absent.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier monitoring schedule: report due, frequency, recipient

title.en: Define how a supplier-notified change to its service is assessed before it takes effect

description.en: Write down the route a change notification arrives by, who assesses its security impact, what makes a change material, and how acceptance or objection is recorded and returned to the supplier. Attach the supplier change procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier service change assessment procedure

title.en: Collect and review each supplier report that fell due in the period

description.en: Chase what did not arrive, read what did, and record the reviewer's conclusion plus any finding raised with the supplier. Attach the received reports with review notes; a missing report is itself a finding and should appear as one.

evidenceHint.en: Received supplier reports for the period with review notes and findings raised

title.en: Log every supplier-notified service change and the impact assessment made on it

description.en: Record each notified change, the date it was received and takes effect, the assessor, the security impact found and the response given. Attach the supplier change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier change log with assessment outcome per change

title.en: Hold the periodic service review with each supplier above the risk threshold

description.en: Cover open findings, incidents affecting the service, changes made since the last review, and delivery against agreed levels. Record the actions agreed, their owners and the target dates. Attach the review record per supplier reviewed.

evidenceHint.en: Supplier service review record with agreed actions and owners

templates.title: Information security for use of cloud services
templates.objective: To ensure the part of cloud security the organisation must provide for itself is identified, configured and checked, and that it can leave a service with its information.
templates.successCriteria:
Each cloud service in use is inventoried with its owner, the classification it holds and the region it runs in.
The split of responsibility with each provider is recorded, so no control rests on the assumption that the other party performs it.
A baseline exists for the organisation's own configuration of each service, and checks against it record every deviation with a disposition.
Services holding business information have an exit plan covering extraction and deletion by the provider, and unapproved cloud found in use has been inventoried.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the cloud service inventory with service, owner, data classification and region.
Collect the shared-responsibility matrix held for each inventoried service.
Gather the customer-side configuration baselines and the exit plans written per service.
Retrieve the baseline check output with its deviations and dispositions.
Obtain the unapproved-cloud review listing services found and their disposition.

Analysis:
Compare the inventory against expense records, single sign-on applications and outbound network destinations to find services in use but uninventoried.
Test the responsibility matrix for controls left unassigned, particularly logging, key management and backup.
Re-run a sample of baseline checks against the live tenant configuration and compare with the recorded result.
Judge whether each exit plan names an extraction format and a deletion confirmation rather than only a notice period.
Check that deviations close with a remediation or an accepted exception instead of carrying forward between periods.

Output:
A list of cloud services in use but absent from the inventory.
Responsibility gaps by service and control area.
Re-run baseline results set against the recorded deviations and their dispositions.

title.en: Compile an inventory of cloud services in use and the information held in each

description.en: Record every SaaS, PaaS and IaaS service, its business owner, the classification of the data held, and the region the data sits in. Attach the cloud inventory; include services paid for by individual teams, not only those procured centrally.

evidenceHint.en: Cloud service inventory: service, owner, data classification, region

title.en: Record the split of security responsibility between the organisation and each cloud provider

description.en: For every inventoried service, state which controls the provider operates and which the organisation must configure or run itself — identity, logging, encryption, backup, patching. Attach the responsibility matrix per service; the organisation's column is the work the remaining tasks act on.

evidenceHint.en: Shared-responsibility matrix per cloud service

title.en: Set the configuration baseline the organisation must apply inside each cloud service

description.en: Cover the customer-side settings the responsibility matrix assigns to the organisation: authentication and MFA, administrative roles, audit logging and its retention, encryption options, and network or public exposure. Attach the baseline for each service.

evidenceHint.en: Customer-side configuration baseline per cloud service

title.en: Write the exit plan for each cloud service holding business information

description.en: State how the information is extracted, in what format, how long extraction takes, and how the provider's copies and backups are deleted on termination. Attach the exit plan per service so a provider change is not blocked by an unanswerable data question.

evidenceHint.en: Cloud exit plan per service, covering extraction and provider-side deletion

title.en: Check each cloud service against its configuration baseline and record deviations

description.en: Run the check on the live tenant rather than from documentation, list every setting that differs from the baseline, and record whether it was corrected or accepted and by whom. Attach the check output per service.

evidenceHint.en: Baseline check output per cloud service with deviations and dispositions

title.en: Search for cloud services adopted outside the approval route and add them to the inventory

description.en: Compare the inventory against sign-ins recorded by the identity provider and against expenditure on cloud vendors, to surface services the inventory does not know about. Attach the review listing each service found and whether it was adopted, migrated or shut down.

evidenceHint.en: Unapproved-cloud review listing services found and their disposition

templates.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation has settled in advance who responds to an incident, by what steps and on what record, so the response is not invented while the incident runs.
templates.successCriteria:
An incident classification scheme is published with its categories, severity levels and worked examples.
Response roles are held by named people with deputies and a contact route that actually reaches them.
A handling procedure runs from detection through to closure and an incident record template captures timeline, actions and evidence.
Exercises are run against the procedure, and their findings together with the review of closed incidents produce amendments to the plan.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the incident classification scheme with its categories, severity levels and examples.
Collect the incident response role assignment sheet naming holders, deputies and contact routes.
Gather the incident handling procedure covering detection through to closure.
Retrieve the incident record template and the fields it requires.
Obtain the exercise record with scenario, participants, timings and gaps, and the review of closed incidents.

Analysis:
Check the named role holders against current staff records and test one contact route rather than reading it.
Walk the handling procedure at one severity level and identify steps with no owner or no condition for moving on.
Compare the template's required fields with what closed incident records actually contain.
Read the exercise record for the gaps it exposed and trace each to an amendment of the procedure or the role sheet.
Establish whether the review of closed incidents examined how the procedure performed, not only how the incident ended.

Output:
A role-by-role confirmation of holders, deputies and reachable contact routes.
A list of procedure steps lacking an owner or a closure condition.
The exercise and review findings with the plan amendment made against each.

title.en: Define what counts as an information security incident and set the severity levels

description.en: Write the categories the organisation will use and a severity scale with a worked example at each level, so someone triaging at 2am can classify without a debate. Attach the classification scheme; escalation and response commitments hang off these levels.

evidenceHint.en: Incident classification scheme with categories, severity levels and examples

title.en: Name the incident response roles and the people who hold them

description.en: Define coordinator, technical lead, communications and the authority who may escalate or declare a major incident, and record the named holder and deputy for each, with an out-of-hours contact route. Attach the role sheet with names against roles, not just role titles.

evidenceHint.en: Incident response role assignment sheet with named holders, deputies and contact routes

title.en: Write the incident handling procedure from detection through to closure

description.en: Set out logging, triage against the severity scale, containment, preservation of evidence, escalation and communication, recovery and closure — with the responsible role named at each step. Attach the procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Incident handling procedure covering detection through closure

title.en: Prepare the incident record template that captures timeline, actions and evidence

description.en: Build the form responders will fill in during an incident: detection time and source, classification, actions with timestamps, evidence collected and where it is held, decisions taken and the closure rationale. Attach the template so the record is not improvised mid-incident.

evidenceHint.en: Incident record template with the required fields

title.en: Run an exercise of the incident procedure and record what it exposed

description.en: Take a realistic scenario through the procedure with the named role-holders, timing each step, and record where the plan was unclear, contacts were unreachable or a step could not be performed. Attach the exercise record with the gaps listed.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise record with scenario, participants, timings and gaps identified

title.en: Review closed incidents for procedure steps that did not work as written

description.en: For every incident closed in the period, note where responders departed from the procedure or found it silent, and record the amendment made to the plan, roles or template as a result. Attach the review with a finding and an outcome against each incident.

evidenceHint.en: Post-incident review with per-incident findings and the resulting plan amendments

templates.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
templates.description: Assess and decide on security events
templates.objective: To ensure every reported event is judged against the same written criteria, and that the decision to declare an incident, or not to, is recorded with its reasoning.
templates.successCriteria:
Severity tiers and the conditions qualifying an event as an incident are written as observable conditions rather than left to judgement.
Reported events land in one queue whatever route brought them in, and classification is a required field on each.
Every event reported in the period carries an assigned tier, the reasoning for that tier and the resulting decision.
A sample of closed events re-assessed against the criteria shows the disagreements found and the correction made for each.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the classification criteria naming each tier, its observable conditions and the threshold at which an incident is declared.
Collect the blank assessment record template together with one completed example.
Gather the queue configuration export showing the intake sources and the mandatory classification field.
Retrieve the event log for the period with one classification, rationale and decision per event.
Obtain the sample re-assessment noting its size, the disagreements found and the corrections made.

Analysis:
Test the intake sources in the configuration against the ways events are actually reported, including verbal and service-desk routes.
Select events from the log and classify them against the criteria independently of the rationale recorded.
Look for events whose rationale restates the tier instead of citing the conditions that decided it.
Examine events sitting near the declaration threshold for a pattern of classification just below it.
Check that the corrections arising from the re-assessment reached the event records themselves.

Output:
An intake coverage statement against the single queue.
Independently classified events set beside the recorded tier, with the disagreements named.
The spread of events around the declaration threshold, with any clustering below it.

title.en: Define the severity tiers and the conditions that qualify an event as an incident

description.en: Write the classification scheme: for each severity tier, state the observable conditions (data exposure, service loss, unauthorised access) that place an event in it, and state the threshold at which an event is declared an incident rather than closed. Attach the criteria document.

evidenceHint.en: Classification criteria document listing each tier, its observable conditions, and the declaration threshold

title.en: Create the assessment record that captures classification, rationale and decision

description.en: Build the record (form or ticket template) an assessor completes for a reported event, with mandatory fields for the tier assigned, the reasoning against the criteria, and the outcome (declared / closed / referred). Attach the blank template and one completed worked example.

evidenceHint.en: Blank assessment template plus one completed example record

title.en: Route reported events into one queue where each carries a classification field

description.en: Wire the reporting channels (helpdesk, monitoring alerts, staff reports) into a single queue so no event is assessed outside the process, and make the classification field mandatory before an item can be closed. Attach the queue configuration and a screenshot showing the required field.

evidenceHint.en: Queue configuration export showing the intake sources and the mandatory classification field

title.en: Record the tier assigned and the reasoning for every reported event

description.en: For each event that arrives in the queue during the period, complete the assessment record: assign a tier against the published criteria, write the reasoning, and log the decision. Events closed without declaration need the same record as those escalated.

evidenceHint.en: Event log for the period showing one classification, rationale and decision per event

title.en: Re-assess a sample of closed events against the criteria

description.en: Take a sample of events closed during the period, apply the criteria independently, and compare the result with the tier originally assigned. Record every disagreement and whether the original decision was corrected or the criteria clarified.

evidenceHint.en: Sample re-assessment noting sample size, disagreements found, and the correction made for each

templates.title: Response to information security incidents
templates.description: Respond to incidents per documented procedures
templates.objective: To ensure a declared incident is contained, eradicated and recovered from by the documented route, by the people the tier names, with the notifications it obliges.
templates.successCriteria:
Each incident category has containment, eradication and recovery steps documented in the order they are taken.
Responders and an escalation contact are named for each severity tier, and the access each responder needs has been confirmed.
Declared incidents carry a timeline with an actor and a timestamp against every action and decision.
Parties the procedure names were notified or the reasoning for not notifying is recorded, and the tabletop's findings produced amendments to the response procedure.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the response procedure with the ordered containment, eradication and recovery steps for each incident category.
Collect the dated responder and escalation contact list with the access confirmation held per named responder.
Gather the timelines recorded for incidents declared in the period.
Retrieve the notification log per incident showing recipient, channel and timestamp, and the reasoning where nothing was sent.
Obtain the tabletop exercise report listing the gaps found and the amendment raised for each.

Analysis:
Match the actions in a declared incident's timeline to the steps its category prescribes, noting steps skipped or taken out of order.
Measure the interval between declaration and the first containment action against what the tier expects.
Verify that each responder's access was confirmed and still holds rather than assumed from their role.
Test the regulatory and contractual notification deadlines that applied against the timestamps in the log.
Assess the reasoning recorded where no notification was sent and whether the person deciding was entitled to.

Output:
A step-by-step comparison of the response taken against the procedure, per sampled incident.
Notification timings set against the deadlines that applied to each incident.
Tabletop gaps with the procedure amendment made against each.

title.en: Document the containment, eradication and recovery steps for each incident category

description.en: For each category the classification scheme produces (malware, account compromise, data exposure, service disruption), write the ordered actions a responder takes, the systems and access needed, and the point at which the incident may be closed. Attach the procedure set.

evidenceHint.en: Response procedure covering each incident category with its ordered response steps

title.en: Name the responders and the escalation contact for each severity tier

description.en: Record who responds at each tier, who they escalate to, and how each is reached out of hours. Confirm each named person has the access the procedure assumes, and attach the contact list with the date each entry was confirmed.

evidenceHint.en: Responder and escalation contact list, dated, with the access confirmation per named responder

title.en: Record the actions, timestamps and decisions taken for each declared incident

description.en: Maintain a running timeline per declared incident: what was observed, what action was taken, by whom, at what time, and the decisions made at each escalation point. The timeline is written during the response, not reconstructed afterwards.

evidenceHint.en: Incident timeline per declared incident, with actor and timestamp on each entry

title.en: Notify the internal and external parties the procedure names for each incident

description.en: For each declared incident, work through the notification list in the procedure — management, affected business owners, customers, regulators or contractual counterparties as applicable — and log who was told, when, and through which channel. Where a party was assessed as not requiring notification, record that assessment.

evidenceHint.en: Notification log per incident showing recipient, channel, timestamp, and the reasoning where no notification was sent

title.en: Run a tabletop exercise of one incident category and record where the procedure failed

description.en: Walk a realistic scenario through the documented steps with the named responders, and capture every point where a step was missing, ambiguous, pointed at a system nobody could reach, or named a person who has left. Raise a correction to the procedure for each.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise report listing the gaps found and the procedure amendment raised for each

templates.title: Learning from information security incidents
templates.description: Learn from incidents to improve security
templates.objective: To ensure knowledge gained from information security incidents is converted into tracked improvements that reduce the recurrence of comparable incidents.
templates.successCriteria:
Every incident meeting the published review threshold has a completed review naming its cause and its contributing factors.
Each cause a review identifies carries an improvement action with a named owner and a current status.
Repeat causes across the period are visible in trend analysis, each with a proposed control change.
Improvement actions recorded as closed are supported by an observed change in the target system.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the post-incident review template and the written threshold stating which incidents require one.
Obtain the incident register for the period and the completed review records it produced.
Collect the improvement action register entries linked to their source incident.
Obtain the period's trend analysis of repeat incident causes.
Gather the verification results for improvement actions recorded as closed.

Analysis:
Compare the incident register against the threshold to find incidents that qualified for a review and did not receive one.
Check that each review names a cause and contributing factors rather than restating the chronology of the incident.
Trace every cause a review identified to an improvement action bearing an owner and a status.
Assess whether the trend analysis counts repeat causes and proposes a control change for each.
Re-perform the verification on a sample of closed actions by inspecting the target system.

Output:
A schedule of qualifying incidents showing which were reviewed within the period.
A traceability listing from review cause to improvement action and its verified state.
A list of repeat causes with no proposed control change and of actions closed without implementation.

title.en: Create the post-incident review format capturing cause and contributing factors

description.en: Define the questions a review must answer: what allowed the incident to occur, what allowed it to continue undetected, what worked in the response, and what changes would reduce recurrence or impact. Attach the format and the threshold of incidents it applies to.

evidenceHint.en: Post-incident review template plus the written threshold stating which incidents require one

title.en: Hold a post-incident review for each incident above the review threshold

description.en: Convene the responders and the affected system owners after closure, work through the review format, and record the causes and contributing factors agreed. A review is complete when the record names causes, not just a narrative of events.

evidenceHint.en: Completed review record per qualifying incident, naming causes and contributing factors

title.en: Raise a tracked improvement action for each cause a review identifies

description.en: Convert every cause recorded in a review into an action with a named owner and a target, entered in the tracker rather than left in the review document. Link each action back to the incident it came from so closure can be traced.

evidenceHint.en: Action register entries linked to their source incident, each with owner and status

title.en: Analyse incident causes across the period for repeat occurrences

description.en: Group the period's incidents by cause and category to find causes that recurred, and state for each repeat whether the earlier improvement action was absent, incomplete, or ineffective. Propose the control change indicated.

evidenceHint.en: Trend analysis naming repeat causes, their incident counts, and the control change proposed for each

title.en: Confirm the improvement actions from earlier reviews were implemented

description.en: Take the actions raised from prior post-incident reviews and check the change actually landed in the system, procedure or configuration named — not merely that the ticket was closed. Record any action closed without the change taking effect.

evidenceHint.en: Verification listing each action, the change observed in the target system, and any closed-but-unimplemented actions

templates.title: Collection of evidence
templates.description: Collect and preserve evidence for incidents
templates.objective: To ensure evidence relating to information security events is acquired and preserved so that its integrity and origin remain demonstrable when it is later relied upon.
templates.successCriteria:
Each evidence type has a documented method for identifying, acquiring and preserving it.
Every collected item carries an unbroken custody record from collection to release, showing handler, time and each transfer.
Acquired items sit in the designated repository under a recorded integrity hash, reachable only by named handlers.
Re-verification reproduces the recorded hash for stored items, and every mismatch has a recorded disposition.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the evidence-handling procedure with the acquisition and preservation method recorded per evidence type.
Obtain the blank chain-of-custody record and the completed custody records for items collected in the period.
Obtain the repository listing showing item identifier, integrity hash and acquisition date.
Obtain the repository access list and the output of the most recent hash re-verification run.

Analysis:
Check the procedure covers every evidence type the organisation can expect to acquire, volatile sources included.
Follow a sample of items through their custody records looking for gaps in handler, time or transfer history.
Reconcile items recorded as collected against the repository listing to find items acquired but never deposited.
Compare the repository access list against the handlers the procedure authorises.
Examine the re-verification output for hash mismatches and confirm a disposition was recorded for each.

Output:
A custody continuity result for each item sampled.
A reconciliation of items collected against items held under a recorded hash.
A statement of hash mismatches and of repository access held outside the authorised handler list.

title.en: Document how each evidence type is identified, acquired and preserved

description.en: For each type the organisation would need to collect (disk images, memory captures, log exports, cloud audit trails, physical media), record the acquisition method, the tooling used, and how the copy is preserved so it stays usable. Attach the procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Evidence-handling procedure with an acquisition and preservation method per evidence type

title.en: Create the chain-of-custody record used for every collected item

description.en: Build the record that travels with an item: unique identifier, what it is, who collected it, when and from where, and a row for each subsequent transfer of custody. Attach the blank record and one completed example.

evidenceHint.en: Blank chain-of-custody record plus one completed example

title.en: Record custody for each evidence item from collection through to release

description.en: Complete a custody record at the moment each item is collected and add a row at every handover, including transfers to external parties. An item with a gap in its custody chain is recorded as such rather than back-filled.

evidenceHint.en: Custody records for the period's collected items, each showing handler, time and transfer history

title.en: Store each acquired item in the designated repository with an integrity hash

description.en: On acquisition, compute a hash of the item, record it against the item identifier, and place the item in the controlled repository with access restricted to the handling team. Attach the repository listing showing item, hash and acquisition date.

evidenceHint.en: Repository listing with item identifier, hash and acquisition date, plus the repository access list

title.en: Re-verify stored evidence against its recorded hash

description.en: Recompute the hash of each item held in the repository and compare it with the value recorded at acquisition. Report every mismatch or missing item, and record what happened to it.

evidenceHint.en: Verification run output listing item, expected hash, observed hash, and the disposition of each mismatch

templates.title: Information security during disruption
templates.objective: To ensure a stated minimum level of security still holds while the organisation runs in a degraded or fallback mode, and that every relaxation is authorised and later reversed.
templates.successCriteria:
Each continuity mode has a recorded list of the controls it degrades or bypasses.
A minimum security requirement is stated for every continuity mode, with the relaxations accepted alongside it.
The fallback environment enforces the access control set for it and its logs reach the central destination.
Every control relaxed during a disruption shows an authoriser, a start time and a confirmed restoration.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of continuity modes with the controls each one degrades or bypasses.
Obtain the minimum security requirements recorded per mode and the relaxations accepted with them.
Obtain the fallback environment configuration export and log samples showing delivery to the central destination.
Obtain the relaxation log for disruptions in the period and the most recent disruption test report.

Analysis:
Compare the modes listed against the continuity plans to find operating modes with no control impact recorded.
Check the fallback configuration against the access control and logging requirements written for that mode.
Trace the log samples to the central destination and confirm they are retained there for the stated period.
Review the relaxation log for entries lacking an authoriser or a restore time, and confirm restoration in the live system.
Compare each stated minimum requirement against the control state the test actually observed.

Output:
A per-mode statement of degraded controls set against the minimum requirements written for them.
A confirmation of the fallback environment's access control and log delivery posture.
A list of relaxations left unrestored and of minimum requirements the test found breached, with remediation per item.

title.en: Identify the security controls bypassed or weakened in each continuity mode

description.en: Walk each continuity and failover arrangement (alternate site, degraded mode, manual workaround, emergency access) and list the controls that stop applying or apply more weakly there — authentication, logging, segregation, monitoring. Attach the resulting list keyed by mode.

evidenceHint.en: List of continuity modes, each with the controls that degrade or are bypassed in it

title.en: Record the minimum security requirements that must hold while operating in fallback

description.en: For each continuity mode, state which of the degraded controls must nevertheless be maintained and to what level, and which relaxations are accepted for the duration of a disruption. Attach the requirements statement with the acceptance for each relaxation.

evidenceHint.en: Minimum security requirements per continuity mode, with the accepted relaxations recorded

title.en: Configure the fallback environment to enforce its access control and logging requirements

description.en: Apply the access restrictions, authentication and log forwarding the requirements demand to the alternate site or degraded-mode systems, so they are in place before a disruption rather than configured during one. Attach the configuration export and the log destination showing events arriving from the fallback environment.

evidenceHint.en: Fallback environment configuration export plus log samples proving events reach the central destination

title.en: Record the authorisation and restoration of every control relaxed during a disruption

description.en: When a control is relaxed or emergency access granted during a disruption, log the control, who authorised it, when it started, and when normal operation was restored. Close the loop by confirming the control is back in force after the event.

evidenceHint.en: Relaxation log with control, authoriser, start time, restore time and the post-event confirmation

title.en: Test a disruption scenario and check the minimum requirements actually held

description.en: Invoke or simulate one continuity mode and observe whether the requirements stated for it were met — was access still restricted, were logs still captured, was segregation preserved. Record each requirement as held or breached, with the remediation for breaches.

evidenceHint.en: Test report comparing each stated minimum requirement to the observed control state, with remediation per breach

templates.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
templates.objective: To ensure ICT services can be restored within the recovery time and recovery point targets that the business processes depending on them actually require.
templates.successCriteria:
Every in-scope ICT service inherits a recovery time and recovery point target from the business process it supports.
Each service has a runbook giving restore steps, dependency order and the check that confirms the restore succeeded.
The backup, replication or standby arrangement provisioned for a service is capable of meeting that service's target.
Exercises record an achieved recovery time and point, and the runbook corrections they prompt are made.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the mapping of ICT services to business processes with the recovery time and point target each service inherits.
Obtain the recovery runbook held for each in-scope service.
Obtain configuration evidence for the backup, replication or standby arrangement behind each service.
Obtain exercise records showing start and finish times with the achieved recovery time and point.
Obtain the most recent reconciliation of runbooks against the ICT architecture.

Analysis:
Check the target held against each ICT service matches the one its business process requires.
Assess whether runbooks state dependency order and a success check, not restore steps alone.
Compare backup frequency, replication lag and standby capacity against the target each is meant to satisfy.
Measure achieved recovery times from the exercise records against target and confirm corrections reached the runbook.
Review the reconciliation for services holding no runbook and for runbooks naming retired systems.

Output:
A service-level table of required against achieved recovery time and recovery point.
An assessment of whether each provisioned arrangement can meet the target set for its service.
A list of services without a current runbook and of exercise corrections still outstanding.

title.en: Map each ICT service to the recovery time and recovery point its business process requires

description.en: Take the recovery objectives set for the business processes and trace them down to the ICT services, data stores and third-party dependencies each process relies on, so every service carries a target it inherited rather than one invented for it. Attach the mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Service-to-process mapping showing the recovery time and recovery point target inherited by each ICT service

title.en: Write the recovery runbook for each ICT service, including dependency order

description.en: For each in-scope service, document the steps to restore it: where the backup or standby lives, the order dependencies must come up in, the credentials and access needed, and how restoration is confirmed successful. Attach the runbook set.

evidenceHint.en: Recovery runbook per in-scope service, showing restore steps, dependency order and the success check

title.en: Provision the redundancy and backup arrangements the recovery targets require

description.en: Where the mapped target cannot be met by the current arrangement, put the standby capacity, replication or backup frequency in place that makes it achievable, and record for each service what was provisioned. Attach the configuration evidence per service.

evidenceHint.en: Per-service configuration evidence of the backup, replication or standby arrangement supporting its target

title.en: Exercise the recovery runbook for an ICT service and record the achieved recovery time

description.en: Run the runbook against a real restore into an isolated environment, timing it end to end and checking the restored data against the recovery point target. Record where the runbook was wrong or incomplete and correct it.

evidenceHint.en: Exercise record with start and finish times, achieved recovery time and point against target, and the runbook corrections made

title.en: Reconcile the recovery runbooks against the current ICT architecture

description.en: Compare the services and dependencies named in the runbooks with those actually running, and find services introduced or re-platformed since the runbooks were written that no plan covers. Record each unmatched service and the runbook raised for it.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing services with no runbook, runbooks referencing retired systems, and the action for each

templates.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
templates.description: Identify and comply with legal requirements
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation knows which legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual security obligations bind it, keeps that knowledge current, and can show each one is satisfied.
templates.successCriteria:
The obligations register names the source instrument, the jurisdiction and the affected service for every entry.
Each obligation is mapped to the controls and system owners that satisfy it, with the unmapped ones listed separately.
Every obligation names a monitoring source and the person watching it for change.
Register amendments record the date, the source that triggered them and the owners notified.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of legal, regulatory and contractual security obligations.
Obtain the obligation-to-control mapping together with the separate list of unmapped obligations.
Obtain the monitoring source and named watcher recorded against each obligation.
Obtain the obligations register change history for the period.
Obtain the compliance assessment of in-scope services against the obligations mapped to them.

Analysis:
Test the register for completeness against contracts signed and jurisdictions entered during the period.
Check the mapped control addresses the requirement the obligation states and that its system owner is in post.
Assess whether each monitoring source would surface a change and whether the watcher is still employed.
Compare register amendments against what the monitored sources published in the period.
Review the compliance assessment for services marked as meeting an obligation without supporting evidence.

Output:
A completeness result for the register against the period's new contracts and jurisdictions.
A list of obligations holding no mapped control, no system owner or no monitoring source.
A gap schedule drawn from the compliance assessment, naming the remediation owner for each gap.

title.en: Compile the register of legal, regulatory and contractual security obligations

description.en: Enumerate the obligations that bear on information security for each jurisdiction the organisation operates in and each service it delivers, drawing from statute, sector regulation and customer contracts. Record for each the source instrument and the part of the business it binds. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Obligations register with source instrument, jurisdiction and affected service per entry

title.en: Map each register entry to the controls and system owners that satisfy it

description.en: For every obligation, name the control, process or system that meets it and the owner accountable for that control, so an obligation with no control behind it becomes visible. Attach the mapping and list the entries that currently map to nothing.

evidenceHint.en: Obligation-to-control mapping, with the unmapped obligations listed separately

title.en: Record the monitoring source that signals a change for each obligation

description.en: For each register entry, name where a change would be noticed — regulator publication, counsel briefing, contract renewal, industry body — and who watches it. This is what keeps the register current rather than a point-in-time snapshot.

evidenceHint.en: Register column or annex naming the monitoring source and the watcher for each obligation

title.en: Amend the register when a monitored source reports a changed obligation

description.en: When a monitored source reports a new or amended requirement, update the affected register entries, re-check the control mapping still satisfies the changed wording, and notify the owners whose controls are affected. Keep the change history rather than overwriting.

evidenceHint.en: Register change history showing the date, the source that triggered it, the requirement amended and the owners notified

title.en: Assess each in-scope service against its mapped obligations and record gaps

description.en: Take the services in the register and test whether the mapped controls are actually operating as the obligation requires, rather than merely assigned. Record each obligation as met or gapped, with the remediation and owner for every gap.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance assessment listing obligation, service, met/gapped status and the remediation owner per gap

templates.title: Intellectual property rights
templates.objective: To ensure software and third-party material are used only within the rights the organisation actually holds, and that the obligations attaching to those rights are honoured on release.
templates.successCriteria:
Every licensed product and third-party item in use appears in the inventory against its licence or purchase record.
Permitted seats, environments and redistribution rights are recorded per licence, and deployed installations stay within them.
Software reaches managed endpoints only through the approved acquisition route and approved repositories.
Each release ships a component manifest with resolved licences and the attribution those licences require.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of licensed software and third-party material with the licence or purchase reference per row.
Obtain the entitlement summary stating permitted seats, environments and redistribution rights per licence.
Obtain the endpoint and repository configuration restricting installation, with the approved acquisition route.
Obtain a recent build's component manifest with resolved licences and the attribution notice shipped with it.
Obtain the entitlement reconciliation and the latest scan for software absent from the inventory.

Analysis:
Check inventory rows carry a licence or purchase reference and that the reference permits the use observed.
Recount installations per product against permitted seats and confirm each over-deployment was actually resolved.
Attempt an install from an unapproved source on a sample endpoint and confirm the restriction refuses it.
Trace manifest dependencies to their resolved licences and check the shipped attribution covers them.
Review the scan output for software found outside the inventory and confirm each item received a disposition.

Output:
A licence position per product giving entitlement, deployed count and the resolution of any excess.
A result on whether installation is confined to the approved acquisition route.
A list of unlicensed or unattributed components found in builds or on endpoints, with the disposition of each.

title.en: Inventory the licensed software and third-party material in use

description.en: List the commercial software, subscriptions, datasets, media and other third-party material the organisation uses, and hold the licence, purchase record or terms of use alongside each entry. Attach the inventory with the source document referenced per row.

evidenceHint.en: Software and third-party material inventory, each row referencing its licence or purchase record

title.en: Record the permitted seats, deployments and redistribution limits for each licence

description.en: Read the terms of each licence held and extract what it actually permits — how many users or installs, which environments, whether the material may be modified or passed to customers — so entitlement can be compared with use. Attach the entitlement summary per licence.

evidenceHint.en: Entitlement summary per licence stating permitted seats, environments and redistribution rights

title.en: Restrict software acquisition and installation to approved sources

description.en: Configure the endpoint and server controls so software arrives through the managed catalogue or approved repositories rather than arbitrary downloads, and route purchase requests through the procurement path that records a licence. Attach the policy configuration and the request route.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint and repository configuration showing the installation restriction, plus the documented acquisition route
