Describe the arrangement as it actually operates, whatever form it takes. Attach the record covering each entry point, including any point where no check is made.

evidenceHint.en: Per-entry-point record of who or what checks entitlement, the refusal handling and the override authority

title.en: Set out the terms on which people without their own entitlement are admitted

description.en: Write down the conditions under which visitors, contractors, delivery and collection staff and anyone else without an entitlement of their own is let into a controlled area: what identification is established, who authorises the admission, whether they are accompanied and by whom, and what is written down when they arrive and when they leave. Attach the admission terms together with the blank form the record will be kept on.

evidenceHint.en: Admission terms for non-entitled people, plus the blank record form they will be entered on

title.en: Record each admission of someone without their own entitlement

description.en: For every person admitted during the period on the terms above, capture the area entered, who authorised the admission, who accompanied them if anyone did, and the times of arrival and departure. Attach the completed admission records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Completed admission records for the period showing area, authoriser, accompaniment and times in and out

title.en: Withdraw entry entitlement when the need for it ends, and record the withdrawal

description.en: When somebody leaves, changes role, or finishes the work that gave them entitlement, remove their ability to enter the areas concerned — recovering whatever they hold that admits them and striking them from the entitlement record — and note the date and who did it. Attach the withdrawal records for the period beside the list of leavers, role changes and completed engagements they answer to.

evidenceHint.en: Withdrawal records for the period, matched to the leavers, role changes and ended engagements they correspond to

title.en: Compare who can actually get in against the entitlement record

description.en: Take each controlled area and establish who is in a position to enter it in practice, then set that against the entitlement record. List everyone who can enter without an entitlement and everyone entitled who no longer needs it, and record what was done about each. Attach the comparison and its outcomes.

evidenceHint.en: Comparison per area listing every discrepancy between actual and recorded entitlement, with its resolution

templates.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
templates.objective: To ensure each room is protected in proportion to what is kept and done inside it, and that its location and contents are not advertised to those outside.
templates.successCriteria:
Each room's record names what it holds and the protection that room is required to provide.
Public indications of where sensitive rooms are and what they contain have been removed or changed.
A room falls short of its required protection only while a dated remediation action is open.
A room found unsecured is recorded with the state it was in and the means by which it was made secure.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the room record naming each room, its holdings, and the protection it is required to provide.
Obtain the record of public indications found and the change made to each, with before and after.
Obtain the per-room remediation record and the period's securing findings.
Obtain the review comparing each room record with how the room is now used.

Analysis:
Walk a sample of rooms and compare what is present with what the record says the room holds.
Test the required protection against the holdings rather than against the room's original designation.
Look for indications the removal record missed: directories, wayfinding, delivery instructions, room booking listings and external signage.
Confirm each securing finding names both the state the room was found in and how it was made secure.
Compare the review's conclusions against the rooms whose use changed in the period, rooms taken on or given up included.

Output:
Room-by-room comparison of recorded holdings with the contents observed.
Listing of surviving public indications and where each was found.
Schedule of rooms below their required protection, with the age of the open action.
Record of rooms whose use changed without a corresponding amendment to the room record.

title.en: Record what each office, room and facility holds and the protection it therefore needs

description.en: Go through the rooms and facilities in use and set down, for each, the information, equipment and activities it contains and, from that, the protection the room itself must provide — how it is closed and fastened, what may be stored in it, whether it may be left unattended, and what separation it needs from neighbouring space. Attach the room record.

evidenceHint.en: Room record naming each room, what it holds and the protection the room is required to provide

title.en: Remove the public indications of where sensitive rooms are and what they hold

description.en: Find where the location or purpose of a sensitive room is announced to people with no need to know it — signage and wayfinding, internal and external directories, published plans, delivery addressing, listings in the organisation's own materials — and change or remove each one. Attach a record of what was found and what was done to it, showing the state before and after.

evidenceHint.en: Record of each public indication found and the change made to it, with before and after

title.en: Bring each room up to the protection its record requires

description.en: Take the rooms whose present state falls short of the room record and settle each shortfall — by providing the storage, fastening, separation or restriction the record calls for, by moving what is held into a room that already meets it, or by revising the requirement with a stated reason and who agreed it. Attach the remediation record per room.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record per room naming the shortfall, the action taken and the date

title.en: Record every room found left open or otherwise not secured as required

description.en: Whenever a room in the record is found unattended without the securing its record calls for — standing open, fastening not engaged, protective arrangement not in use — note the room, who found it, when, what was not secured, and how the room was made secure again. Attach the findings for the period, including the occasions on which nothing was found.

evidenceHint.en: Securing findings for the period naming the room, the state it was found in and how it was made secure

title.en: Check each room record against how the room is now used

description.en: Rooms change hands and change purpose. Go through the room record and confirm, room by room, that what it says the room holds is still true and that the protection stated is still the protection needed; where it is not, say what changed and raise an action. Attach the review listing the rooms whose holdings or required protection have moved, with the action raised for each.

evidenceHint.en: Review listing the rooms whose holdings or required protection changed, with the action raised for each

templates.title: Physical security monitoring
templates.objective: To ensure unauthorised presence is observed while it is happening and reaches somebody able to act, and that what the monitoring captures is itself protected.
templates.successCriteria:
The monitoring record names how and when each watched area is observed, and which areas are deliberately left unwatched.
Each kind of observation has a named recipient, a route to them, and an expected action.
Captured material is kept for a stated period and viewed only by those currently on the permitted list.
Every observation of possible unauthorised access is logged with its responder, its finding and its outcome.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the monitoring record of watched areas, the means of observation, the hours covered, and the areas left unwatched.
Obtain the response record naming the recipient, route and expected action for each kind of observation.
Obtain the retention and access statement for monitoring material with the current list of permitted viewers.
Obtain the period's monitoring log and the verification record for each monitored area.

Analysis:
Compare the watched areas against the areas the organisation treats as controlled and confirm each gap was a decision rather than an omission.
Generate an observation in one area and follow it to the named recipient, timing its arrival against the action expected.
Compare the permitted viewer list with the accounts and keys that can in fact reach the captured material.
Test retention by requesting material from the start of the stated period and material older than it.
Read the verification record for faults found and confirm each was repaired rather than simply logged.

Output:
Coverage map of watched and unwatched areas set against the controlled areas.
Timed trace of one observation from capture to the responder who acted on it.
Comparison of permitted viewers with actual access to captured material.
Schedule of monitoring faults, their repair dates, and the periods an area went unwatched.

title.en: Record which areas are watched for unauthorised access and how each is watched

description.en: Set down the areas, entry points and approaches kept under observation for people being where they should not be, and for each one how that observation is achieved and when it applies — continuously, out of hours, on rounds. Name plainly any area in scope that is not watched at all. Attach the monitoring record.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring record naming each watched area, how it is observed, when, and the areas left unwatched

title.en: Record who is told when something is observed, and what they are to do

description.en: For each kind of observation the monitoring can produce — somebody in an area out of hours, an entry forced or held open, an unaccompanied stranger, an area that should be occupied standing empty — set down who is told, by what route, and what they are expected to do, including the point at which they pass it to somebody else. Attach the response record covering every kind of observation.

evidenceHint.en: Response record per kind of observation, naming the recipient, the route and the action expected

title.en: Record how what the monitoring captures is kept and who may see it

description.en: State where the material the monitoring produces is held, how long it is kept before disposal, who is permitted to view or release it and on what grounds, and how a request to view it is authorised and recorded. Attach the statement together with the current list of people permitted to view.

evidenceHint.en: Retention and access statement for monitoring material, with the list of people currently permitted to view it

title.en: Record every observation of possible unauthorised access and how it was dealt with

description.en: Capture each occasion during the period on which the monitoring produced something needing a response, including the ones that turned out to be innocent: what was observed, where, when, who responded, what they found, and how it ended. Attach the log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring log for the period, each entry with the observation, the responder, the finding and the outcome

title.en: Confirm each area is still being watched the way its record says

description.en: Take the monitoring record area by area and establish that the observation it describes is actually happening now — that rounds are being made where rounds are the arrangement, that what should be in view is in view and not obstructed, that what should be captured is being captured, and that it reaches the person named in the response record. Note every arrangement found not working and the repair made. Attach the verification record.

evidenceHint.en: Verification record per monitored area, with how it was checked, the faults found and their repair

templates.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
templates.objective: To ensure the hazards each site is genuinely exposed to are answered by a protection somebody owns, or stand as exposures the organisation has knowingly accepted.
templates.successCriteria:
Each site's exposure record names its threats, the areas and assets exposed, and the effect expected.
Every recorded threat maps to a protection with an owner, or is named as unprotected.
Threats left uncovered end in a protection introduced or an exposure accepted by a named decider.
Every protection register row is accounted for in the period by a test, a service result, a condition check, or the provider's evidence.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain each site's exposure record with its threats, the areas and assets exposed, and the expected effect.
Obtain the protection register linking every threat to the protection in place and its owner.
Obtain the decisions recorded against the threats the register leaves uncovered.
Obtain the period's evidence that each protection still stands, and the reassessment against changes at and around each site.

Analysis:
Test the exposure record against the site's surroundings, services and history rather than against a generic threat list.
Account for every protection register row in the period's evidence and identify the rows supported by nothing.
Where the evidence is a provider's, confirm it covers the organisation's own equipment and areas rather than the building generally.
Where the protection is an inherent condition, confirm somebody checked the condition is unchanged instead of assuming it.
Read each accepted exposure for the decider's authority to accept it and for a date on which the acceptance is revisited.

Output:
Threat-to-protection matrix per site, with the owner and the evidence relied on this period.
Listing of protection register rows with no evidence for the period.
Schedule of accepted exposures, their decider, and their revisit date.
Record of changes at and around each site since the last assessment, with their effect on exposure.

title.en: Record the physical and environmental threats each site is exposed to

description.en: For every site, set down the natural and man-made threats it could suffer — fire, water, storm, ground movement, extremes of temperature, explosion or damage arising from activity nearby, disruption of the surrounding area — reasoning from the site's location, construction, neighbours and history. For each threat, record what would be affected and how badly. Attach the exposure record per site.

evidenceHint.en: Exposure record per site naming each threat, the areas and assets exposed and the effect expected

title.en: Map each recorded threat to the protection that answers it

description.en: Take the exposure record and set against each threat whatever already stands between it and what it would affect — construction, separation, distance, detection, suppression, drainage, containment, or an arrangement with somebody else to act — and name who is responsible for keeping that protection working. Name plainly every threat with nothing against it. Attach the protection register.

evidenceHint.en: Protection register linking each threat to the protection in place and its owner, with unprotected threats named

title.en: Settle each threat the protection register leaves uncovered

description.en: For every threat the register names as having nothing against it, record the outcome reached: the protection introduced, the reduction of what is exposed at that site, or a stated decision to accept the exposure with the reason and the name of whoever accepted it. Attach the record covering every uncovered threat, referencing the register rows it clears.

evidenceHint.en: Record per uncovered threat of the protection introduced or the exposure accepted, with who decided and when

title.en: Show that each protection against the site's threats still stands

description.en: Work down the protection register and record, for every entry, what was done or observed during the period to establish that the protection is still doing its job. Where the protection is something that operates — a detector, a suppression system, a pump, a barrier that has to be worked — that is the inspection, test, service, replenishment or replacement, with the date, who did it, the result, and any fault raised and its repair. Where the protection is inherent in the site — its construction, the level it sits at, the distance or open ground between it and the hazard — that is a confirmation that the condition is unchanged, with the date and who checked. Where somebody else provides it, attach what they supplied. Attach the record for the period with every register row accounted for.

evidenceHint.en: Record for the period accounting for every protection register row: the service or test result, the confirmation the inherent condition is unchanged, or what the provider supplied

title.en: Reassess site exposure against the changes made at and around each site

description.en: List what changed at or around each site during the period — building work, a change of use, new neighbouring activity, an event that actually occurred and what it did — and say for each whether it alters the exposure record or the protection register. Update both where it does, and raise an action wherever the protection no longer matches the exposure. Attach the reassessment.

evidenceHint.en: Reassessment naming each change, its effect on exposure, and the register updates or actions raised

templates.title: Working in secure areas
templates.description: Define procedures for working in secure areas
templates.objective: To ensure people inside a secure area know how they are required to behave there, and that work done alone or by outsiders is visible after the fact.
templates.successCriteria:
Each secure area records the work carried out in it, the roles performing that work, and the equipment taken in.
The conduct rules state which secure areas each rule covers.
Every person working in a secure area has a dated record of how the rules were given to them.
Work by people from outside the organisation and work done alone are logged with the activity and the person accountable.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the activity record per secure area: the work performed, the roles performing it, and the equipment taken in.
Obtain the secure-area conduct rules together with the mapping of each rule to the areas it covers.
Obtain the awareness records naming person, area, date and the means by which the rules were given.
Obtain the secure-area work log for outsiders and lone workers, and the check report on observed conduct.

Analysis:
Compare the recorded activities with what the area is equipped for and identify work happening there that the record does not mention.
Test the equipment-taken-in entries against what is actually present in the area, recording and imaging devices included.
Match everyone who worked in a secure area during the period against the awareness records and examine the unmatched names.
Check the work log for cases where the accountable person was themselves from outside the organisation.
Read the check report for departures observed and confirm the action taken addressed the person as well as the rule.

Output:
Listing of activities observed in secure areas that the activity record omits.
Comparison of secure-area workers with awareness records, naming those holding none.
Schedule of outsider and lone-work entries with the person accountable for each.
Record of observed departures from the conduct rules and the action taken on each.

title.en: Record the work carried out inside each secure area and who performs it

description.en: For every area the organisation treats as secure, write down what work actually happens inside it, which roles perform that work, what equipment or materials are taken in to do it, and whether any of it is done by people from outside the organisation or by someone working alone. Build this from asking the people who use the area rather than from an assumption about its purpose. Attach the activity record, one section per secure area.

evidenceHint.en: Activity record per secure area naming the work, the roles performing it and the equipment taken in

title.en: State the rules of conduct that apply inside each secure area

description.en: Turn the activity record into written rules for behaviour inside the area: what may be brought in and what may be taken out, the position on recording and capture of what is visible there, when work may proceed without a second person present, what applies to people from outside the organisation, and what must be done when the area is left with nobody in it. Write a rule only where the activity record shows the situation arises. Attach the rules with the areas each one covers.

evidenceHint.en: The secure-area conduct rules, showing which areas each rule covers

title.en: Record how each person working in a secure area is made aware of its rules

description.en: For every person who works in a secure area — employed or not — record that the rules for that area were put in front of them before they first worked there, by whatever means the organisation uses, and hold their confirmation that they received them. Attach the awareness record naming the person, the area, the date and the means used, covering everyone the activity record says works there.

evidenceHint.en: Awareness record naming person, area, date and the means by which the rules were given

title.en: Log the work done in secure areas by people from outside the organisation and by people working alone

description.en: Keep a running record of each occasion someone from outside the organisation, or someone working without a second person present, carries out work inside a secure area. Capture the area, the work done, the person, who was accountable for them while they were inside, and the period they were there. Attach the log covering the reporting period.

evidenceHint.en: Secure-area work log for the period, with area, worker, activity and the person accountable

title.en: Check observed conduct in secure areas against the stated rules

description.en: Attend secure areas while work is under way, without giving notice, and compare what is actually being done against the rules written for that area — what has been brought in, whether work that needs a second person has one, whether the area is left as the rules require. Record each departure from the rules, who it was raised with and what changed. Attach the check report.

evidenceHint.en: Check report listing each departure from the rules observed and the action taken

templates.title: Clear desk and clear screen
templates.description: Implement clear desk and screen policy
templates.objective: To ensure an unattended workspace or screen gives nothing away, wherever the work is done and whatever material happens to be passing through it.
templates.successCriteria:
The scope list covers desks, shared points and screens, naming what is handled at each and the storage available there.
The rules state, situation by situation, what must be put away and what a screen must show when left unattended.
Each area records where its unattended material is secured, and any area without an answer is named.
Each class of screen has a recorded means of becoming unreadable and the setting or instruction behind it.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scope list of workspaces, shared points and screens with what is handled at each and the storage available.
Obtain the published clear desk and clear screen rules as written per situation.
Obtain the per-area record of where unattended material is secured and the per-class record of what makes a screen unreadable.
Obtain the check records from workspace walks and the results of the sample screen test.

Analysis:
Compare the scope list with the floor as it now stands, taking in printers, scanners, post trays, meeting rooms and hot desks.
Test whether the storage in each area can actually hold the material handled there, and read the areas recorded as unresolved.
Take a screen from each class and confirm it becomes unreadable by the recorded means within the stated interval, rather than reading the setting alone.
Compare what the walks found exposed with the material the scope list says that area handles.
Follow each unresolved area to an action, an alternative arrangement, or a change in what is handled there.

Output:
Scope list annotated with the workspaces and shared points found on the floor but not listed.
Per-class screen results: the means recorded, the interval observed, and whether the screen became unreadable.
Listing of areas whose storage cannot hold the material handled in them.
Record of what each walk found exposed, set against that area's handled material.

title.en: List the desks, shared points and screens the clear desk rules must cover

description.en: Walk the places where people work and where information ends up waiting: fixed and shared desks, meeting and interview rooms, print and collection points, post trays, whiteboards, and any screen that faces a space the organisation does not control. For each, note what kind of information is handled there and what is available today for putting it away. Attach the resulting scope list.

evidenceHint.en: Scope list of workspaces, shared points and screens, with what is handled at each and the storage available

title.en: State what must be put away and what a screen must show when a workspace is left unattended

description.en: Write the rules against the situations in the scope list rather than as a general principle: a desk left at the end of the day, a desk left for a short period, a meeting room vacated, output waiting at a collection point, a whiteboard after a discussion, a screen left with nobody in front of it. Say for each what must not remain visible or reachable. Attach the published rules with the situation each covers.

evidenceHint.en: Published clear desk and clear screen rules, written per situation

title.en: Record where the material held at each workspace is put when it is left unattended

description.en: Go through the scope list and, for every area, record the destination its papers and portable items go to when the workspace is left — a container at the desk, a room used for the purpose, a return to a central holding point, or a rule that such material is not handled there at all. Where the recorded destination did not exist, record what was provided or what handling changed instead. Attach the per-area record with any area still unresolved.

evidenceHint.en: Per-area record naming where unattended material is secured, and the areas still unresolved

title.en: Record how each class of screen is made unreadable when left unattended

description.en: For every class of workstation, shared terminal and fixed display in scope, record what makes the screen unreadable once nobody is in front of it — an unattended period after which it locks itself, an action the user is required to take, sign-out at a shared machine, or how the display is positioned — and the setting or instruction that delivers it. Attach the record covering every class in the scope list, including any class nothing currently reaches.

evidenceHint.en: Record per screen class of what makes it unreadable when unattended and the setting or instruction behind it

title.en: Record what is found left exposed when workspaces are checked

description.en: Walk the areas in scope while they are unoccupied and note what has been left in view or within reach against the rules for that situation: documents, portable items, keys, whiteboard content and unattended screens. Record the area, what was found, what was done with it and the follow-up with whoever left it. Attach the record of each check made in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Check record per walk, naming the area, what was found exposed and the follow-up

title.en: Check that screens are in fact unreadable by the means recorded for their class

description.en: Take a sample of screens across every class in the screen record and establish, for each, whether it is genuinely unreadable when nobody is in front of it — testing it the way its own record says it works. Where the record relies on an unattended period, leave the screen and wait it out. Where it relies on an action the user takes, take screens their users have left and see whether the recorded instruction produced an unreadable screen. Where it relies on signing out at a shared machine, look at what that machine shows between users. Where it relies on how the display faces, read it from the space it can be seen from. Include screens that sit outside whatever normally applies the class, since those are the ones most likely to differ. Attach the sample check listing each screen, how it was tested, what was found and whether it matched its class record.

evidenceHint.en: Sample check listing each screen, how it was tested against its class record, the result observed and whether it matched

templates.title: Equipment siting and protection
templates.objective: To ensure that information-processing equipment is placed where the hazards of its surroundings cannot damage it, disturb its operation, or expose the information it handles.
templates.successCriteria:
Every item of processing equipment appears in the siting register with its room or rack location and the hazards observed there.
Each equipment class has stated placement conditions, and items that breached them were repositioned or shielded with sign-off.
No installation or move completes without a siting check, and the register is updated from the move log.
Floor inspections find no equipment standing in a location the register does not describe.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the siting register and the hazard recorded against each equipment location.
Obtain the siting standard giving the acceptable placement conditions per equipment class.
Collect the remediation records for items repositioned or shielded, with their sign-offs.
Pull the equipment move and install log for the period.
Obtain the inspection sheets comparing the floor against the register.

Analysis:
Trace a sample of equipment from the inventory to a register row carrying a location and a hazard.
Test each sampled item's placement against the conditions its class requires and note the breaches.
Confirm every breach recorded has a remediation entry naming the action taken and a sign-off.
Check that each move log entry carries a siting check outcome and a matching register update.
Compare inspection deviations against their resolutions to see whether the register was corrected.

Output:
Siting conformance findings per sampled equipment item.
A list of moves completed without a recorded siting check.
A statement of register-to-floor discrepancies still open.

title.en: Map the physical location of every item of information-processing equipment

description.en: Walk each site and record, for every server, network device, workstation, printer and screen, the building, room and rack or desk it occupies. Note alongside each entry the hazards present at that spot: overlooking from public areas, water pipes overhead, external windows, proximity to loading or delivery routes, heat sources. Attach the completed siting register as evidence.

evidenceHint.en: Siting register listing each equipment item, its room/rack location, and the hazards observed at that location

title.en: Record the siting rules that apply to each class of equipment

description.en: Write down, per equipment class and location type, what siting is acceptable: screen orientation away from windows and public sightlines, minimum clearance from water and drainage runs, restriction of rack rooms to authorised entry, separation from delivery and loading areas. Ground each rule in a hazard actually observed in the siting register rather than a generic list. Attach the siting standard.

evidenceHint.en: Siting standard giving the acceptable placement conditions per equipment class

title.en: Reposition or shield the equipment whose placement breaches the siting rules

description.en: Take the register entries that fail the siting standard and fix each one: move the unit, rotate or fit a privacy filter to the screen, install a drip tray or deflector, or relocate the rack. Where a move is not possible, record the compensating measure fitted. Evidence is a remediation record per non-conforming item showing the before state, the action taken and who signed it off.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record per non-conforming item with the action taken and sign-off

title.en: Check the siting rules on every equipment installation or move

description.en: Make the siting check a recorded step in the equipment move and install process: before the unit is powered on at its new spot, the engineer records the location, confirms it against the siting standard and updates the siting register. Run this for every move in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Equipment move and install log for the period, each entry carrying the siting check outcome and the register update

title.en: Inspect each equipment location against the siting register

description.en: Walk the sites again and compare what is physically present against the register: equipment that has moved without a record, new units not registered, screens that have been turned, shielding that has been removed. Record each deviation and how it was resolved. Attach the inspection sheet with the deviation list.

evidenceHint.en: Inspection sheet listing deviations found between the floor and the register, with resolution per deviation

templates.title: Security of assets off-premises
templates.objective: To ensure that assets taken beyond the premises stay accounted for and carry protection matched to the information they hold for as long as they are away.
templates.successCriteria:
Every asset permitted to leave the premises is registered with its holder, authorised destination type and information classification.
Each off-premises asset class has stated protective measures, and no asset departs without a recorded check-out approval.
The check-out log shows removal, holder, approver and return date for each departure in the period.
Reconciliation accounts for every registered asset as returned, still authorised out, or raised as unaccounted.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the off-premises asset register with holder, destination type and classification per asset.
Obtain the handling standard mapping protective measures to each off-premises asset class.
Collect the check-out form or workflow definition and the completed check-out records.
Pull the check-out log covering the period under test.
Obtain the reconciliation of the register against returned and outstanding assets.

Analysis:
Check that each registered asset carries a named holder and a classification the standard recognises.
Test the measures required for a sampled asset class against what the holder actually applied while away.
Verify that sampled removals were approved before departure by the approver the workflow names.
Trace log entries to returns and confirm overdue items appear in the reconciliation.
Assess whether unaccounted assets were escalated and resolved rather than left open.

Output:
An exception list of assets removed without a recorded approval.
Overdue and unaccounted asset findings with their resolution status.
A view of register accuracy measured against the check-out log.

title.en: List every asset authorised to be taken off the premises and who holds it

description.en: Enumerate the laptops, mobile devices, portable media, and any equipment issued for home working, travel or client sites. For each, record the holder, the type of destination it is authorised for, and the classification of information it carries or can reach. Attach the off-premises asset register.

evidenceHint.en: Off-premises asset register: asset id, holder, authorised destination type, information classification

title.en: Record the protection required for each class of off-premises asset

description.en: State per asset class what must be in place before it leaves: full-disk encryption, screen lock timeout, privacy filter, physical lock, the rule on leaving equipment unattended in vehicles or hotel rooms, and what the holder does if it is lost. Derive the classes from the register rather than writing a generic mobile-working policy. Attach the handling standard.

evidenceHint.en: Off-premises handling standard mapping each required protective measure to an asset class

title.en: Set up the check-out approval step for removing an asset from the premises

description.en: Put in place the form or workflow that captures, before an asset leaves, who is taking it, where, for how long, and the approval. Include the confirmation that the protections required for that asset class are in place. Attach the form or workflow configuration together with one completed example.

evidenceHint.en: The check-out form or workflow definition plus one completed check-out record

title.en: Record each asset removal and return in the check-out log

description.en: For every asset that leaves and comes back during the period, log the removal date, holder, destination, approver and the return date. Keep items still signed out visible as open entries so custody is known at any moment. Attach the log covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Check-out log for the period showing removal, holder, approval and return date per asset

title.en: Reconcile the off-premises register against assets actually returned or still signed out

description.en: Compare the check-out log with the register and with physical or remote confirmation of each asset: items shown as returned that cannot be located, items long overdue, holders who have changed role. Record each discrepancy and what was done about it. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of the register against the check-out log, listing overdue and unaccounted assets and their resolution

templates.title: Storage media
templates.objective: To ensure that storage media are protected in proportion to the information they carry, from the point they are registered until that information is no longer recoverable.
templates.successCriteria:
The media register names every medium held with its type, its holder or location, and the classification of the information on it.
Handling rules exist per media type and classification, and media already held meet them or carry an accepted alternative.
Every transfer is entered in the register so custody passes between named holders without a gap.
Withdrawn media have a closed entry naming what became of the item and what shows its information is unrecoverable.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the media register with type, location and classification per medium.
Obtain the handling rules covering protection, storage, identification, transfer and withdrawal.
Collect the per-item alignment records and the exceptions with their accepted alternative handling.
Pull the register movement entries and the withdrawal entries for the period.
Obtain the reconciliation of registered media against media physically present.

Analysis:
Match a sample of registered media to the handling rule its type and classification invoke.
Verify each exception was accepted by an authorised party and states the alternative applied.
Follow a sampled transfer chain and confirm a releasing and a receiving holder is named at every step.
Test withdrawal entries for a stated reason, a disposition and proof that the information cannot be read back.
Examine reconciliation discrepancies for a resolution rather than an adjustment of the register alone.

Output:
Handling-rule conformance findings per sampled medium.
A list of custody gaps found in the movement entries.
Unresolved discrepancies between registered and present media.

title.en: Record every storage medium held, where it is and what information is on it

description.en: Enumerate the media the organisation holds as items in their own right — backup and archive media, portable drives, memory devices, cards, and disks that have been taken out of the equipment they served. Include media held away from the organisation's own sites and media carried in field or engineering kit. For each, record its identifier, its type, who holds it or where it sits, and the classification of the information written to it. Attach the media register.

evidenceHint.en: Media register: identifier, type, holder or location, and the classification of the information held

title.en: State the handling each media type and classification requires

description.en: For each combination of media type and information classification appearing in the register, write down what is required: how the information on it is protected against being read by someone who obtains the item, where it is kept when not in use, how it is identified so a holder knows what they have, how it is accompanied and tracked when it moves between holders or locations, and the point at which it must be taken out of use. Attach the handling rules.

evidenceHint.en: Media handling rules giving the protection, storage, identification, transfer and withdrawal requirement per type and classification

title.en: Bring the media already held into line with the handling rules

description.en: Work down the register item by item and record what was done to bring each one to the handling its type and classification calls for — how its information was protected, how it was identified, and where it was moved to. Where an item cannot meet the rule, record it as an exception with the handling put in its place and who accepted that. Attach the per-item record showing the state of every entry in the register.

evidenceHint.en: Per-item record showing what was applied to each registered medium, and each exception with its accepted alternative handling

title.en: Record each transfer of media so custody is unbroken

description.en: Log every movement in the period against the register entry it affects: a medium given to a person, moved between locations, sent to or recalled from a holding site, or handed to whoever carries it. Each entry names who released it, who received it and when, so the register can answer who holds any item at any moment. Attach the movement entries for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Media register movement entries for the period, naming releasing and receiving holder at each step

title.en: Close the register entry for each medium withdrawn from use

description.en: When a medium reaches the point of withdrawal the handling rules set, or fails before it, record why it was withdrawn, what became of the item, and what is held to show the information it carried can no longer be recovered from it, then mark the register entry closed. Run this so no withdrawn medium is left as an open entry. Attach the withdrawal entries for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Withdrawal entries for the period, each naming the reason, what became of the item and what shows its information is unrecoverable

title.en: Account for every medium the register lists

description.en: Confirm the presence of each open register entry at the location or with the holder it names, and identify media found that the register does not list. Record every difference — present but unregistered, registered but not found, held by someone other than the recorded holder — and how each was resolved. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of registered against present media, listing each discrepancy and its resolution

templates.title: Supporting utilities
templates.objective: To ensure that the supplies each processing facility depends on are protected, watched by someone on duty, and sized for the load the facility now carries.
templates.successCriteria:
Each facility has a dependency list naming every supporting supply, its provider or route, and its rated capacity.
Every dependency is mapped to the protective equipment fitted, and dependencies left unprotected are named rather than omitted.
Utility failure alarms reach a monitored destination, proven by a test alert received by the on-duty recipient.
Protective equipment carries dated test results, and measured load is compared with rated protection so shortfalls are owned.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the utility dependency list per facility with provider or route and rated capacity.
Obtain the mapping of each dependency to its protective equipment, including those named as unprotected.
Collect the alarm configuration export and the record of the test alert being received.
Pull the UPS, generator, cooling and sensor test records for the period.
Obtain the capacity assessment comparing measured load against rated protection.

Analysis:
Confirm the dependency list covers every in-scope facility and that no supply is missing from it.
Check rated runtime or capacity against the load the mapped equipment would have to carry.
Verify the alarm destination was staffed when the test alert arrived and that receipt was logged.
Review test records for missed intervals, failed measurements and whether faults raised were closed.
Assess each shortfall in the capacity assessment for an agreed action and a named owner.

Output:
A coverage statement of dependencies protected against those left exposed.
Utility test findings including missed tests and failed measurements.
Capacity shortfall findings per facility with owner and agreed action.

title.en: List the supporting utilities each information-processing facility depends on

description.en: For every site and equipment room, record the utilities it needs to keep running: mains feeds and their supply routes, HVAC and ventilation units, water and drainage, telecommunications circuits and their carriers. Note the rated capacity or supply limit of each. Attach the utility dependency list per facility.

evidenceHint.en: Utility dependency list per facility naming each supply, its provider or route, and its rated capacity

title.en: Record the protective equipment fitted against each utility dependency

description.en: Map each dependency in the list to what protects it: UPS units and their rated runtime, generators and fuel held, redundant power feeds, standby cooling, diverse telecoms routes. Where a dependency has no protection, record it as such rather than leaving it blank. Attach the mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Mapping of each utility dependency to its protective equipment, with rated runtime or capacity, and the unprotected dependencies named

title.en: Route utility failure alarms to a monitored destination

description.en: Configure the alarms on power, cooling and environmental sensors so a failure or threshold breach reaches somebody who is on duty — building management system, monitoring platform or paging rota. Trigger a test condition and confirm the alert was received. Attach the alarm configuration and the received test alert.

evidenceHint.en: Alarm configuration export plus evidence of a test alert being received by the on-duty destination

title.en: Record each utility inspection and protective-equipment test result

description.en: Run the inspections and load tests due in the period — UPS discharge, generator run, cooling service, sensor check — and record the date, the result including measured runtime or capacity, and any fault raised. Attach the test and inspection records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: UPS, generator, cooling and sensor test records for the period with dates, measured results and faults raised

title.en: Assess whether utility protection still covers each facility's current load

description.en: Compare the present electrical and cooling load of each equipment room against the rated capacity and the runtime measured in testing. Where load has grown past what the protection covers, record the shortfall and the action agreed. Attach the assessment.

evidenceHint.en: Capacity assessment comparing measured load against rated protection per facility, with shortfalls and agreed actions

templates.title: Cabling security
templates.objective: To ensure that the power and network cabling serving each facility is documented, identifiable end to end, protected where it is exposed, and free of connections nobody authorised.
templates.successCriteria:
A route plan or schedule exists per facility showing entry points, routes, patch rooms and the circuits each run carries.
Cables and patch panel ports carry labels matching the identifiers the schedule assigns them.
Segments and patch rooms found exposed have protection fitted and recorded against the segment concerned.
Patching changes appear in the change log with their schedule update, and inspections leave no undocumented or unlabelled cable in place.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the cable route plan or schedule per facility with entry points, routes and circuits carried.
Collect the labelling records or patch panel photographs showing the schedule identifiers.
Obtain the remediation records naming each exposed segment or patch room and the protection fitted.
Pull the patching change log for the period and the schedule updates it produced.
Obtain the inspection records covering patch rooms and accessible cable runs.

Analysis:
Compare a sample of physical patch panel ports against the identifier the schedule assigns them.
Determine whether every segment judged exposed has a fitted protection recorded against it.
Test whether patching entries reached the schedule, and whether the schedule shows changes the log does not.
Review inspection findings for undocumented cables and confirm each carries a disposition.
Assess whether repeat findings in the same patch room were treated as a recurring cause.

Output:
Label-to-schedule conformance results per sampled port.
A list of schedule entries out of step with the patching log.
Undocumented cable findings with the disposition recorded for each.

title.en: Map the power and network cable routes serving each facility

description.en: Record where cabling runs: building entry points, risers, floor voids and ceiling runs, patch rooms and cabinets, and the circuits each route carries. Note where power and data share a route and where cable passes through areas outside the organisation's control. Attach the cable route plan or schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Cable route plan or schedule showing entry points, routes, patch rooms and the circuits carried

title.en: Label the cables and patch panel ports to match the cable schedule

description.en: Apply labels at both ends of each run and on every patch panel port so a cable can be identified without tracing it. The labels must use the same identifiers as the schedule. Attach photographs or a labelling record per patch panel and cabinet.

evidenceHint.en: Labelling record or photographs per patch panel showing labels matching the cable schedule identifiers

title.en: Protect the cable routes and patch rooms identified as exposed

description.en: Address the routes flagged in the mapping: fit conduit or trunking to accessible runs, lock patch cabinets and comms rooms, separate power from data cabling where induction or damage is a risk, and secure building entry points. Record what was fitted for each exposed segment. Attach the remediation record.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record naming each exposed cable segment or patch room and the protection fitted

title.en: Record each patching change against the cable schedule

description.en: Every time a port is patched, repatched or a run is added or removed, log the port, the circuit, the reason and the date, and update the cable schedule in the same step so the schedule stays true. Attach the patching log for the period alongside the updated schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Patching change log for the period with the corresponding cable schedule updates

title.en: Inspect patch rooms and accessible cable runs for undocumented connections

description.en: Physically inspect cabinets, risers and accessible runs looking for cables not on the schedule, unlabelled patches, taps or splitters, and unsecured cabinet doors. Record each unidentified cable and whether it was traced, removed or added to the schedule. Attach the inspection record.

evidenceHint.en: Inspection record listing every undocumented or unlabelled cable found and its disposition

templates.title: Equipment maintenance
templates.objective: To ensure that equipment is serviced at the intervals its continued availability depends on, by parties bound to stated conditions, with missed services visible and recovered.
templates.successCriteria:
The maintenance schedule names each item needing service, its responsible party or agreement, the interval with its basis, and the next due date.
Maintenance conditions are documented and cited by clause in every agreement covering listed equipment.
Each job in the period is filed against its equipment item with date, performer, work done and any condition raised.
Items repaired off site hold release and return records showing the information decision taken and the return or open status.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the maintenance schedule with service intervals, the basis for each and the next due dates.
Obtain the maintenance conditions document and the supplier clause references that bind it.
Pull the maintenance records for the period filed against individual equipment items.
Collect the release and return records for equipment repaired away from the organisation.
Obtain the overdue-service report for the period.

Analysis:
Test whether the interval set for a sampled item follows the supplier or manufacturer basis recorded.
Confirm each supplier servicing listed equipment is bound by a clause that cites those conditions.
Trace sampled jobs from the schedule to a filed record and check that conditions raised were followed up.
Verify off-site repairs recorded a decision about the information held before the item was released.
Evaluate overdue services for a stated availability consequence and an agreed recovery date.

Output:
Interval conformance findings per sampled equipment item.
A list of suppliers servicing equipment without a binding conditions clause.
Overdue-service findings with recovery dates and the items still outstanding.

title.en: Record which equipment must be serviced to stay available and when each service falls due

description.en: Identify the items the organisation depends on for its information processing that will degrade or fail without servicing, and for each record who is responsible for that servicing — an internal team or a named supplier and the agreement covering it — the interval at which it is to be serviced, what that interval was set from, and the date the next service falls due. Attach the maintenance schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance schedule: item, responsible party or agreement, service interval and its basis, next due date

title.en: State the conditions that apply to anyone servicing equipment and to the information it holds

description.en: Write down what governs work on the equipment in the schedule, whether it is done on site, remotely or after the item is taken away: how the person doing the work is confirmed to be who they claim, what access to the information held on the item the work requires and what they may do with it, whether the item or the storage inside it may leave the organisation's control, and what must be recorded when the work finishes. Where a supplier does the work, record where these conditions are written into the agreement with them. Attach the conditions with those references.

evidenceHint.en: The maintenance conditions document, with the clause references binding each supplier that services listed equipment

title.en: Record each maintenance job against the equipment it was carried out on

description.en: For every service carried out in the period, capture the date, who performed it, what was done, what was replaced, and anything the work revealed about the item's condition. File each record against the item in the schedule, so one item's history can be read in one place rather than assembled from separate reports. Attach the maintenance records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance records for the period filed against each item, with date, performer, work done and condition raised

title.en: Record the release and return of each item sent away for repair

description.en: For every item that leaves the organisation's control to be repaired, record what was done about the information held on it before it went — taken out, put beyond recovery, or left in place under the conditions that bind whoever receives it — together with who took it, when, and the date it came back or was written off instead. Keep items not yet returned visible as open entries. Attach the release and return records for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Release and return records for items repaired away from the organisation, showing the information decision and the return date or open status

title.en: Report the services that fell due and were not carried out

description.en: Compare the due dates in the schedule against the maintenance records for the period and list every service that did not happen when it should have. For each, record why it slipped, what running that item unserviced means for the availability it supports, and the date agreed to bring it back into schedule. Attach the report with those agreed dates.

evidenceHint.en: Overdue-service report naming each missed service, the reason, the availability consequence and the agreed recovery date

templates.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
templates.objective: To ensure that no equipment is released or returned to use until the information in every storage component it holds has been made unrecoverable and that outcome verified.
templates.successCriteria:
Equipment awaiting disposal or re-use is queued with its asset id, the storage components inside it, and the data classification.
A sanitisation standard maps each storage type and classification to a required method and the verification it demands.
Every device leaving the organisation holds an asset-level verification record: tool output, erase confirmation or destruction certificate.
The disposal register names a recipient and date per item, and retired assets reconcile to sanitisation and disposal records.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the disposal queue listing asset ids, the storage components held and the data classification.
Obtain the sanitisation standard mapping storage type and classification to method and verification.
Collect the per-device verification records: tool output, erase confirmations and destruction certificates.
Pull the disposal register with recipients, dates and the contractor receipt or reissue record per asset.
Obtain the reconciliation of retired inventory assets against sanitisation and disposal records.

Analysis:
Check that queued items list every storage component they contain, secondary and embedded storage included.
Test whether the method applied to a sampled device is the one its storage type and classification require.
Confirm verification names the asset id rather than resting on a batch reference alone.
Match each register destination to a contractor receipt or a reissue record for the same asset.
Investigate retired assets carrying no sanitisation record as potential uncontrolled releases.

Output:
Sanitisation method conformance findings per sampled device.
A list of assets disposed of without asset-level verification.
Reconciliation gaps between the retired inventory and the disposal records.

title.en: List the equipment awaiting disposal or re-use and the storage it contains

description.en: Identify every retired or pending-reissue item currently held — laptops, servers, disks pulled from arrays, network devices with configuration in flash, printers and multifunction devices with internal drives. Record the asset id, the storage components inside it, and the classification of data that reached the device. Attach the disposal queue.

evidenceHint.en: Disposal queue listing asset id, the storage components held inside each item, and the data classification

title.en: Record the sanitisation method required for each storage type and classification

description.en: State which method applies to which media and classification: multi-pass overwrite, cryptographic erase where the device was encrypted from first use, degaussing, or physical destruction. Include embedded storage such as printer drives and device flash, and say what verification counts as proof for each method. Attach the sanitisation standard.

evidenceHint.en: Sanitisation standard mapping storage type and data classification to the required method and its verification

title.en: Verify and record the sanitisation of each device before it leaves the organisation

description.en: Apply the method the standard requires, then capture the proof: the wipe tool's completion report, the crypto-erase confirmation, or the destruction certificate with serial numbers. Hold the item until that record exists, so nothing leaves on trust. Attach the verification records referencing asset ids.

evidenceHint.en: Per-device sanitisation verification record — tool output, erase confirmation or destruction certificate — referencing the asset id

title.en: Record the destination of every item disposed of or returned to use

description.en: Log where each item went: the recycler or disposal contractor and their receipt, the leased-equipment return, or the internal reissue and its new holder. Keep the receipt or transfer note against the asset id so the chain does not end at the loading bay. Attach the disposal register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Disposal register for the period with recipient, date and the contractor receipt or reissue record per asset

title.en: Reconcile the disposal register against the assets retired from the inventory

description.en: Take every asset marked retired, reissued or written off in the period and confirm each has a matching sanitisation verification and a recorded destination. Record assets retired with neither, and how each gap was closed. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of retired assets against sanitisation and disposal records, listing gaps and their resolution

templates.title: User endpoint devices
templates.objective: To ensure that the devices people use to hold and reach organisational information are known, configured to a stated standard, and cut off from that information when the user leaves.
templates.successCriteria:
Every device holding or reaching organisational information is inventoried with holder, OS version, ownership and management state.
Each device class has a settings block stating the security configuration it is required to run.
Disk encryption and screen lock are enforced on enrolled endpoints, with any exception annotated in the console export.
Enrolment and de-enrolment entries tie to their joiner or leaver event, and no unmanaged or orphaned device is left without a disposition.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the endpoint inventory with holder, OS version, ownership and management state per device.
Obtain the endpoint configuration standard and the settings block it sets for each device class.
Pull the device-management console export showing encryption and lock state with exceptions annotated.
Collect the enrolment and de-enrolment log for the period with its linked joiner and leaver events.
Obtain the reconciliation of the inventory against the management console.

Analysis:
Compare the console's device population with the inventory and identify what appears in only one of them.
Test a sampled device's live settings against the block its class assigns it.
Check encryption and lock exceptions for an approver and an expiry rather than a standing waiver.
Trace leavers in the period to a de-enrolment entry and measure the delay between the two.
Assess whether orphaned devices found at reconciliation were wiped, recovered or written off.

Output:
Configuration conformance findings per sampled device class.
A list of devices present in the console but absent from the inventory, and the reverse.
Leaver de-enrolment timing findings and the orphaned devices still open.

title.en: Inventory the endpoint devices that hold or reach organisational information

description.en: Enumerate every laptop, desktop, tablet and phone used for work, recording holder, operating system version, and whether it is corporate-owned or personal. Pull the list from the device-management console and reconcile it with HR's headcount so unenrolled devices surface. Attach the inventory itself.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint device inventory listing holder, OS version, ownership and management state per device

title.en: Record the required security configuration for each class of endpoint device

description.en: Write down, per device class in the inventory (corporate laptop, mobile, personal device), what must be true: disk encryption, screen-lock timeout, patch level, malware protection, and whether local administrator rights are permitted. State the reasoning where a class is treated differently. Attach the configuration standard.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint configuration standard, one settings block per device class

title.en: Enforce disk encryption and screen lock on every enrolled endpoint

description.en: Apply the standard's encryption and lock settings as policy in the device-management platform rather than device by device, then export the per-device compliance state and drive the non-compliant devices to compliance. Attach the export plus a note on any device that could not be brought into line and why.

evidenceHint.en: Device-management console export showing encryption and lock state per device, with exceptions annotated

title.en: Record enrolment and de-enrolment of endpoints as users join and leave

description.en: For each period, capture which devices were enrolled and which were wiped or de-enrolled, tied to the joiner or leaver that triggered it. This is what shows a departed user's device stopped reaching organisational information. Attach the log.

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint enrolment and de-enrolment log for the period, each entry linked to its joiner or leaver event

title.en: Reconcile the endpoint inventory against the device-management console

description.en: Compare the inventory to the devices actually reporting in, and list devices present in one and not the other. For each discrepancy record the disposition — enrolled, retired, or accepted with a reason. Attach the reconciliation, not just a statement that it was done.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation showing unmanaged and orphaned devices with a disposition against each

templates.title: Privileged access rights
templates.objective: To ensure that elevated access is held by named people for an authorised purpose and duration, kept apart from everyday accounts, and withdrawn once it is no longer justified.
templates.successCriteria:
Every in-scope system has its privileged accounts and administrative roles registered with the privilege granted and a named holder.
Each privileged role states who authorises it and how long a grant is allowed to last.
Administrators hold a privileged identity separate from the standard account they use for everyday work.
Grants, revocations and break-glass invocations each carry their authorisation, and recertification has removed the accounts it could not justify.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the privileged access register naming system, account or role, privilege granted and holder.
Obtain the rules document mapping each privileged role to its approver and its grant duration.
Pull the directory export pairing administrators' standard accounts with their privileged identities.
Collect the grant and revocation log for the period, including break-glass invocations.
Obtain the recertification record and evidence of the removals it called for.

Analysis:
Compare live privileged group membership in a sampled system against the register.
Test whether sampled grants were authorised by the named approver and ended at the stated duration.
Identify shared or unattributable privileged accounts that trace back to no named holder.
Review break-glass invocations for a justification recorded afterwards and a closing revocation.
Verify that accounts marked for removal at recertification were actually disabled or deleted.

Output:
Register-to-directory differences per sampled system.
A list of privileged accounts holding no named holder or no expiring grant.
Recertification removals called for set against removals completed.

title.en: Inventory the privileged accounts and administrative roles in every in-scope system

description.en: For each system, list the accounts and roles that can change configuration, grant access, or read data across users — including cloud console roles, database superusers, domain administrators, and shared or break-glass accounts. Record the holder for each. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Privileged access register: system, account or role, privilege granted, named holder

title.en: Record who authorises each privileged role and for how long it is held

description.en: Against each role in the register, state who may approve a grant, whether the grant is standing or time-bound, and the conditions for use of break-glass accounts. Where a role is standing, record why time-bounding is not workable. Attach the resulting privileged-access rules.

evidenceHint.en: Privileged access rules document mapping each role to its approver and grant duration

title.en: Separate privileged accounts from their holders' everyday user accounts

description.en: Give each administrator a distinct identity for privileged work so routine email and browsing never run with elevated rights, and remove privilege from the day-to-day account. Attach a directory export showing the pairing, and note any system that cannot support separation together with the compensating measure.

evidenceHint.en: Directory export pairing each administrator's standard account with a separate privileged identity

title.en: Record each grant and revocation of privileged access with its authorisation

description.en: Log every elevation and removal as it happens, capturing who requested it, who approved it, the system, and the date it was withdrawn. Break-glass use is logged the same way with the reason for invoking it. Attach the log covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Privileged access grant and revocation log for the period, including break-glass invocations

title.en: Recertify every privileged account against the register and withdraw those no longer justified

description.en: Put the current holder list for each privileged role in front of the system owner, have them confirm or reject each holder, and remove the rejected ones. Record what was removed and when, so the recertification shows an outcome rather than a signature. Attach the recertification with removals evidenced.

evidenceHint.en: Recertification record showing confirm or remove per privileged account and the completed removals

templates.title: Information access restriction
templates.description: Restrict access to information per policy
templates.objective: To ensure that people reach only the information their role is permitted to read or change, including by bulk export, and that every change to those rules traces to an authorisation.
templates.successCriteria:
An access matrix states read, write or no access for each information class against each role.
System permissions implement the matrix row they correspond to, evidenced per system.
Bulk export and reporting of restricted information is confined to a named list of roles.
Every access-rule change in the period carries a requester and an approver, and account testing reports each deviation found with its correction.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the access matrix of information classes against roles with the access allowed in each cell.
Collect the per-system permission exports placed beside the matrix rows they implement.
Obtain the configuration record of bulk export and reporting rights and the roles that retain them.
Pull the access-rule change log for the period with its requesters and approvers.
Obtain the access test results per sampled account: expected access, actual access and correction.

Analysis:
Check that the matrix covers every information class in scope and leaves no cell undecided.
Compare a sampled system's permission export with its matrix row and note grants that go beyond it.
Test whether the bulk export path enforces the same restriction as the record-level permissions do.
Verify that change log entries name an approver who is not also the requester.
Assess deviations found in account testing for a correction that was applied rather than accepted.

Output:
Matrix-to-permission differences per sampled system.
A list of roles holding bulk export rights outside the named list.
Deviation findings per sampled account with the correction status of each.

title.en: Map each class of information to the roles permitted to read and to change it

description.en: Build a matrix whose rows are information classes or repositories and whose columns are business roles, marking read, write and no-access in each cell. Agree it with the owner of each information class rather than deriving it from what access currently exists. Attach the matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Access matrix of information classes against roles, showing read, write or no access per cell

title.en: Configure system permissions so each role sees only what its matrix row allows

description.en: Translate the matrix into the actual permission model of each system holding the information — groups, roles, sharing settings — and remove access that exceeds the row. Attach a permission export per system alongside the matrix row it implements, so a reviewer can compare them.

evidenceHint.en: Per-system permission export placed beside the matrix row it implements

title.en: Restrict bulk export and reporting of restricted information to named roles

description.en: Identify the routes that yield information in bulk — report builders, database query tools, data exports, integration credentials — and limit them to the roles the matrix permits, so read access to a record does not become read access to the population. Attach the configuration showing who retains bulk export.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration record of bulk export and reporting rights, listing the roles that retain them

title.en: Record every access-rule change against the request that authorised it

description.en: As permissions are granted, altered or withdrawn, log the system, the principal, what changed, who asked and who approved. This is what makes an unexpected permission traceable later. Attach the change log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Access-rule change log for the period, each entry carrying its requester and approver

title.en: Test a sample of accounts against the access matrix and report the deviations

description.en: Pick accounts across several roles, enumerate what each can actually reach in the live systems, and compare it to the matrix row for that role. Record every deviation with its cause — stale grant, over-broad group, matrix wrong — and the correction made. Attach the test results.

evidenceHint.en: Access test results per sampled account: expected access, actual access, deviation and correction

templates.title: Access to source code
templates.objective: To ensure that source code, and every copy of it kept elsewhere, is reachable only by the people and services that currently need it for work in hand.
templates.successCriteria:
The source code register lists each holding and each copy kept outside it, with its owner and its location.
A permission model names who may read, change and administer each holding, non-human identities included.
Holdings enforce the recorded permissions, and access that went beyond them has been withdrawn and listed.
Grants and withdrawals in the period are logged, and reconciliation shows every holder and copy as still needed or removed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the source code register covering each holding and each copy kept outside it.
Obtain the permission model naming read, change and administer holders, human and non-human.
Collect the per-holding permission listings taken after alignment, with the withdrawn access recorded.
Pull the source code access change log for the period, service accounts and tokens included.
Obtain the reconciliation of access holders and copies against current need.

Analysis:
Search build systems, backups and developer workstations for code copies the register omits.
Compare a sampled holding's live permissions with the model and quantify the surplus.
Check whether non-human identities hold change or administer rights where a read right would serve.
Trace logged grants back to a request and logged withdrawals to a leaver or a role change.
Assess whether copies judged unnecessary at reconciliation were deleted rather than left in place.

Output:
A list of code copies found outside the register.
Permission surplus findings per sampled holding, split by human and non-human identity.
Reconciliation outcomes naming the copies and accounts still awaiting removal.

title.en: Register the source code holdings and every copy kept outside them

description.en: Work outward from the code the organisation builds and runs: name each store that holds it and the owner of that store. Then record the copies living outside those stores — working copies on developer machines, archived or escrowed snapshots, and code handed to a third party — because a copy carries none of the store's restrictions with it. Attach the register with one row per holding and per copy.

evidenceHint.en: Source code register: each holding and each copy, with its owner and location

title.en: Record who may read, change and administer each source code holding

description.en: For every row of the register decide three separate things: who may read the code, who may change it, and who may alter the holding's own permissions and settings. Cover non-human identities explicitly — build, deployment and integration accounts hold change rights and are the ones usually left off the model. Attach the permission model.

evidenceHint.en: Permission model naming read, change and administer holders per holding, including non-human identities

title.en: Apply the recorded permissions at each holding and withdraw the access beyond them

description.en: Set each holding's permissions to match the model by whatever means that holding provides, and remove access exceeding the model rather than leaving it noted as an exception. Where a holding cannot express the model, record the restriction relied on instead and who owns it. Attach the resulting permission listing per holding together with the record of what was withdrawn.

evidenceHint.en: Per-holding permission listing after alignment, with the list of access withdrawn
